2027-01-01.title: The Holy Name of Jesus (Circumcision of our Lord) · New Year's Day
2027-01-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God changes Abram's name and gives the covenant of circumcision
I have called you by name, you are mine
The name that is above every name
2027-01-01.alt: Also the First Friday of Nativity, which in this calendar is the last Friday of Nativity: the Divine Motherhood of Mary (Exodus 15:11–21; Acts 1:12–14; Romans 16:17–20, 25–27; Luke 1:39–45). New Year readings: Exodus 23:14–17; Isaiah 52:7–12; Ephesians 4:17–24; Matthew 6:25–34. Weekday readings: Hebrews 1:1–4; John 1:14–18.
2027-01-01.verse: She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
theo: On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and “he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” The Syro-Malabar Church begins the civil year with this feast of the Holy Name. In the first reading God changes Abram's name to Abraham and gives him the covenant sign; a new name means a new mission. Through Isaiah God says to his people: “I have called you by name, you are mine.” Names in the Bible are not labels; they reveal who someone is before God.

The name Jesus, Yeshua, means “the LORD saves”. The angel explains it to Joseph: “he will save his people from their sins.” And St Paul sings the hymn of Philippians: the Son emptied himself, took the form of a slave, became obedient to death on a cross, “Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend.” The way to the exalted Name passed through humility and the Cross.

Today is also the last Friday of the Nativity season, kept as the Divine Motherhood of Mary. The woman who gave the Child his human flesh is the Mother of God; she stands with the Apostles in prayer at the beginning of the Church (Acts 1:14). As the new year opens, the Church places on our lips the Name in which there is salvation, and under our eyes the Mother who keeps us close to her Son.
conn: Circumcision on the eighth day.
Genesis 17:12 commands it as the sign of the covenant. By submitting to the Law, the Son of God enters fully into the history of his people (Galatians 4:4).
Naming.
In Israel the father named the child. Joseph obeys the angel and names him Jesus, thus legally adopting him into David's line (Matthew 1:25).
The Name in Syriac prayer.
The East Syriac liturgy is full of the name Isho Mshiha, Jesus the Messiah. The Malayalam ഈശോ comes from this Syriac form.
Prayer of the Name.
The Jesus Prayer, “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner”, is loved in the Christian East as a way of praying without ceasing.
Divine Motherhood.
The Syro-Malabar calendar keeps the Divine Motherhood of Mary on the last Friday of the Nativity season. The Council of Ephesus (431) confessed Mary as Mother of God.
New Year.
The Church blesses time. Exodus 23:14–17 tells Israel to keep festivals for the Lord through the year: the calendar itself becomes worship.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Name of Jesus is invoked again and again. We receive the One whose Name means “the Lord saves”.
Begin the year by receiving Holy Communion with this prayer: Jesus, be my Saviour this year in every day.
outline: Ask: who gave you your name, and what does it mean?
God names Abraham and calls his people his own.
The meaning of the name Jesus.
Humility and the Cross lead to exaltation.
Joseph whispering the name Jesus over the Child.
live: Pray the Name
Pray the Jesus Prayer slowly ten times each morning this year.
Honour the Name (Philippians 2:10)
Bow your head at the name of Jesus, and never use it carelessly.
Bless the year
Gather your family tonight and consecrate the new year to Jesus under the protection of Mary.
Know your name
Find out the meaning of your baptismal name and the saint you are named after.
fathers: St Bernard of Clairvaux
The name of Jesus is honey in the mouth, music in the ear, joy in the heart.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
His name is a treasure: whoever calls on it is rich, and whoever holds it is not poor.
magis: Prayer to Jesus by name; the Jesus Prayer.
Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.
Mary in the mystery of Christ and the Church.
saints: 2 Jan: First Saturday of Nativity. 3 Jan: Second Sunday of Nativity; St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan: Denha.
2027-01-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, your Name means “the Lord saves”. At the beginning of this new year we bow before your holy Name, which is above every name. Write your Name on our hearts, save us from our sins, and keep us all through this year under the mantle of your Mother, the Mother of God. To you be glory with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-03.title: Second Sunday of Nativity
2027-01-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The skin of Moses' face shone
Speak, for your servant is listening
Present your bodies as a living sacrifice
I must be in my Father's house
2027-01-03.alt: 3 January is also the feast of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (Genesis 12:1–4; Isaiah 44:1–4; 1 Peter 4:12–19; Matthew 5:1–12); where it is kept, follow the local direction. The feast of Denha is on Wednesday 6 January: remind the faithful.
2027-01-03.verse: And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
theo: The two Sundays of Nativity look at the Child growing up. Today's readings are all set in the presence of God. Moses comes down from forty days on Sinai and does not know “that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.” The boy Samuel, sleeping in the temple where the ark was, hears the Lord call him three times, until he learns to answer: “Speak, for your servant is listening.” Those who stay near God are changed by him and learn to listen.

In the Gospel Jesus, at twelve, goes up to Jerusalem for the Passover and stays behind. After three days of anxious searching, Mary and Joseph find him in the Temple, “sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.” His first recorded words are: “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” The Son knows who his Father is. Yet he goes down to Nazareth “and was obedient to them”, and grows “in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.” Holiness and ordinary obedience belong together.

St Paul turns this into a programme for every Christian: “present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship. Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds.” The Temple is now our life offered to God. The feast of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara today shows a son of our Church who lived this: priest, founder, educator, a man of prayer whose face, like Moses', shone with God among his people.
conn: Moses' veil.
Exodus 34 says Moses veiled his face after speaking to the people. St Paul reads this in 2 Corinthians 3: in Christ the veil is removed and we are transformed from glory to glory.
Samuel in the temple.
Samuel was dedicated by his mother Hannah (1 Samuel 1). The lamp of God had not yet gone out: God speaks before the darkness falls.
Bar mitzvah?
The later Jewish rite of coming of age at thirteen is not described in Luke, but at twelve Jesus is close to the age of religious responsibility.
Three days.
Mary and Joseph search for three days before finding Jesus. The Fathers saw a hint of the three days of the Passion before the Resurrection.
First words.
Jesus' first words in Luke speak of his Father; his last words on the Cross also speak to the Father (Luke 23:46).
St Chavara.
St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (1805–1871), co-founder of the CMI and founder of the CMC congregations, pioneered schools beside churches and printed Malayalam books at Mannanam. Canonised in 2014.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is our presence in the Father's house. Like the boy Jesus, we are where we belong.
At the offertory we place ourselves on the altar as a living sacrifice (Romans 12:1). We return home transformed.
outline: Ask: have you ever lost a child in a crowd? What did you feel?
“I must be in my Father's house.”
live: Listen like Samuel (1 Samuel 3:10)
Begin your prayer this week with the words: Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.
Find Jesus in the Father's house
Make a short visit to the church on a weekday.
Obedience at home (Luke 2:51)
Children: obey your parents promptly this week. Parents: listen to your children's questions.
Imitate St Chavara
Support a poor child's education this year.
fathers: St Ambrose (in substance)
The Lord at twelve begins to show that he is the Son of God, and yet he is subject to his parents, so that we may learn obedience.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
He who was greater than the Temple sat in the Temple, listening and asking, so that the teachers might learn who was teaching them.
magis: The hidden life at Nazareth; the finding in the Temple.
Listening to the Word, like Samuel.
saints: 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan: Denha (Baptism of the Lord). 8 Jan: St John the Baptist (First Friday of Denha).
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, at twelve you were found in your Father's house, listening and asking. Then you went down to Nazareth and were obedient. Teach us to listen like Samuel, to shine with God's presence like Moses, and to offer our lives as a living sacrifice. Through the prayers of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, make our homes and our parish places where you grow in us. Glory to you with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-06.title: Denha · The Epiphany and Baptism of our Lord
2027-01-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The Lord descends upon Mount Sinai
I will pour out my spirit on all flesh
Grace revealed through the appearing of our Saviour
You are my Son, the Beloved
2027-01-06.alt: Important feast and day of obligation. The Third Qudasha (anaphora) is used in the Holy Qurbana. Beginning of the Season of Denha.
2027-01-06.verse: And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
theo: Denha is a Syriac word meaning dawn, rising, manifestation. The Eastern Churches celebrate on this day not first the Magi but the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God shone out: the Son in the water, the Spirit descending like a dove, the Father's voice from heaven. “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.” At the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed, and the public ministry of Jesus begins. The Sun of Justice rises over the world.

The readings show God coming down. At Sinai “the LORD had descended upon it in fire”, with thunder, smoke and trembling, and the people had to keep their distance. At the Jordan the heavens are “torn apart”, and God comes close in gentleness: the Spirit descends like a dove upon a man standing in the water among sinners. Joel's promise begins to be fulfilled: “I will pour out my spirit on all flesh.” What was terrifying at Sinai becomes intimate at the Jordan.

Jesus did not need baptism; he was without sin. He went down into the water to sanctify the waters for us and to stand with sinners. St Paul tells Timothy to “rekindle the gift of God that is within you”, for grace “has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light.” Our ancestors' customs, the lamps on plantain stems with the cry “El Paiya”, God is light, and the night bath recalling the Jordan, were ways of saying: our Baptism made us children of light. Denha calls each of us to remember our Baptism and to live as beloved sons and daughters.
conn: Denha.
Syriac for dawn or rising. The feast is called Denha (Epiphany) in the East Syriac tradition, and in Kerala popularly Pindikuthi in the north and Rakkuli in the south.
Pindikuthi.
Lamps were fixed on a plantain stem (pindi) and the family processed around it crying “El Paiya”, a Syriac-Malayalam cry meaning God is light. Christ is the light of the world.
Rakkuli.
On the eve, families bathed in rivers or ponds at night (rakkuli, “night bath”), recalling the Jordan. It was a religious act of remembering Baptism, not a magical rite.
Sinai and Jordan.

Both are theophanies. At Sinai God gives the Law in fire; at the Jordan he gives his Son and his Spirit. Mark says the heavens were “torn apart” (schizō), the same verb used for the Temple curtain at Jesus' death (Mark 15:38).
Blessing of water.
In many Eastern Churches water is solemnly blessed at Denha, because Christ sanctified the waters by his baptism (CCC 1224).
The Fridays of Denha.

On the Fridays of this season the Church remembers the great witnesses of Christ: John the Baptist, Peter and Paul, the Evangelists, Stephen, the Greek and Syrian Fathers, and finally all the faithful departed.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today, with its rich prayers on the Holy Trinity. At the Jordan the Trinity was revealed; at the altar the Trinity gives us the Body and Blood of the Son by the Spirit.
In Baptism we went down into the water with Christ; in the Holy Qurbana we are fed as beloved children.
outline: Ask: do you know the date of your Baptism?
From Sinai's fire to the Jordan's dove.
Jesus sanctifies the waters for us.
Live as beloved children of light.
A plantain stem with small lamps, and a family crying “El Paiya”.
live: Remember your Baptism
Find out your baptismal date and keep it like a birthday.
Bless with holy water
Keep holy water at home and bless yourself and your children each night.
Rekindle the gift (2 Timothy 1:6)
Use one gift God gave you to serve the parish this month.
Keep the custom
Teach children the meaning of Pindikuthi and Rakkuli.
fathers: St Ephrem the Syrian
Fire and Spirit are in the river in which you were baptised: the Jordan received the One who is fire, and the waters were made holy.
St Gregory Nazianzen
Christ is baptised: let us go down with him, so that we may also rise with him.
magis: Baptism makes us children of God and members of the Church.
The Eastern liturgy as a feast of light and theophany.
saints: 8 Jan: First Friday of Denha, St John the Baptist. 10 Jan: Second Sunday of Denha.
2027-01-06.prayer: O Christ, Sun of Justice, today you rose upon the world at the Jordan. The Father bore witness to you and the Spirit descended upon you. Sanctify us who were baptised into you; rekindle in us the gift of God; and let us live as beloved children of light. To you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be praise and glory, now and always and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-10.title: Second Sunday of Denha
2027-01-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The greatness and compassion of God
Who is and who was and who is to come
2027-01-10.verse: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but I speak these things as the Father instructed me.
theo: Denha is the season of manifestation: who is this Jesus revealed at the Jordan? Today's readings answer with the name of God. At the burning bush Moses asks God's name, and God answers: “I AM WHO I AM… Thus you shall say to the Israelites, ‘I AM has sent me to you.’” God is not one being among many; he is the One who simply is, the source of all that exists. Sirach marvels at this God: “He who lives forever created the whole universe”, and yet “the compassion of the Lord is for every living thing.”

In the Gospel Jesus takes up this name. “You are from below, I am from above… you will die in your sins unless you believe that I am he.” In Greek he says simply egō eimi, “I am”. And he adds: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he.” The full manifestation of who Jesus is will happen on the Cross. The God who said “I AM” to Moses hangs on the wood for us, and there his glory shines.

The Book of Revelation gives the same name in the language of praise: “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, “who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.” Jesus Christ is “the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead”, the one “who loves us and freed us from our sins by his blood”. In the Holy Qurbana we worship this Lord, present among us. To believe that Jesus is “I AM” is to build our lives on the only foundation that does not pass away.
conn: The divine name.
The Hebrew YHWH, “I AM”, was considered too holy to pronounce. Jews read Adonai, “Lord”. When Jesus says “I am” in John (8:24, 28, 58), his hearers understand the claim.
Seven “I am” sayings.
John's Gospel has seven “I am” sayings with images: bread, light, gate, shepherd, resurrection, way, vine. Here Jesus uses the absolute “I am”, without an image.
Lifted up.
In John “lifted up” means both crucified and glorified (3:14; 12:32). The Cross is the throne where the I AM is revealed.
Alpha and Omega.
The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet. In the Latin rite they are traced on the Easter candle: Christ is the beginning and end of time.
Sirach.
Ben Sira wrote in Jerusalem about 180 BC. The Church reads this book as Scripture; its Latin title is Ecclesiasticus, “the church book”.
East Syriac prayer.
Our Qurbana often praises God as “the One who is”, holy and incomprehensible, who yet comes near in Christ.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we stand before the One who is. The I AM of the burning bush is present on the altar under the signs of bread and wine.
Revelation calls Jesus the one who loves us and freed us by his blood. At Communion we receive that love and that blood.
outline: Ask: how would you answer if someone asked “Who is God?”
Point 1 · I AM WHO I AM
God's name at the burning bush.
The Cross reveals who he is.
The Lord of all time loves us.
A bush burning but not consumed.
“Then you will realize that I am he.”
live: Adore the One who is
Spend ten minutes in adoration this week, repeating: You are, Lord; I am yours.
Believe (John 8:24)
Make an act of faith each morning: Jesus, I believe that you are the Lord.
Look at the Cross
Place a crucifix where you see it daily, and look at it when you are anxious.
Praise the Alpha and Omega
Begin and end each day with the Glory Be.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)
God said “I AM WHO I AM” because he does not change; we pass, he remains. Cling to him and you will remain.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
The One who is beyond all names took a name among us, that we might call on him and live.
magis: God reveals his name: I AM.
Lifted up on the Cross, Christ draws all to himself.
saints: 14 Jan: St Devasahayam. 15 Jan: Second Friday of Denha, Sts Peter and Paul.
2027-01-10.prayer: O Lord our God, you revealed your holy name to Moses: I AM WHO I AM. In your Son you have shown us your face. Grant that we may believe that Jesus is the Lord, lifted up on the Cross for us, the Alpha and the Omega, and so not die in our sins but live with you. To you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, be glory, now and always and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-17.title: Third Sunday of Denha
2027-01-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Joshua is chosen: be strong and bold
I have chosen you and not cast you off
I press on toward the goal
2027-01-17.alt: Season of Denha. The Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu) begins tomorrow, Monday 18 January: remind the faithful. The Church Unity Octave also begins tomorrow.
2027-01-17.verse: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
theo: The theme of this Sunday is election: God chooses. Moses, old and about to die, calls Joshua before all Israel: “Be strong and bold… it is the LORD who goes before you. He will be with you; he will not fail you or forsake you.” Through Isaiah God speaks to his discouraged people in exile: “You are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you off; do not fear, for I am with you.” To be chosen by God is not a privilege to boast about; it is a mission, and God's presence is its strength.

In the Gospel crowds come from everywhere, and then Jesus goes up the mountain and “called to him those whom he wanted”. He appoints the Twelve. Paul tells the Philippians what being chosen did to him: everything he once counted as gain, his birth, his zeal, his law-keeping, he now regards as loss “because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.” He has not arrived: “forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.”

Tomorrow we begin the Three Days' Fast, the Rogation of the Ninevites, much loved in our Church. It is a time to answer God's choice with conversion, prayer and fasting. The chosen are called not to sit back, but to press on.
conn: Election in the Bible.
God chooses Abraham, Israel, David, the prophets, the Twelve, not because they are better, but for a mission to others (Deuteronomy 7:7–8; CCC 60, 781).
Joshua.
His name, Yehoshua, means “the LORD saves”; it is the same name as Jesus. Joshua leads the people into the promised land, as Jesus leads us into the Kingdom.
The Twelve.
Twelve recalls the twelve tribes: Jesus is gathering a renewed Israel. Mark lists Simon Peter first and Judas last (3:16–19).
Paul's résumé.
Circumcised on the eighth day, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Pharisee, blameless under the law (Philippians 3:5–6). All this he counted as loss for Christ.
Moonnu Nombu.

The Three Days' Fast of the Ninevites is kept in the East Syriac tradition from the sixth century, when a plague in Persia was ended after the people fasted and prayed. It begins on Monday to Wednesday of the third week before the Great Fast (in 2027, 18–20 January).
Kuravilangad.
In Kerala, Kuravilangad Marth Mariam church is especially famous for its Moonnu Nombu pilgrimage and the ship procession (kappal pradakshinam) recalling Jonah's voyage.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the priest prays for those whom God has called to every ministry in the Church. We too are chosen to be a priestly people.
The Body of Christ received at the altar is our strength to press on toward the goal.
outline: Ask: have you ever been chosen for something important? How did it feel?
Joshua chosen; God goes before him.
Israel in exile: do not fear.
Paul strains forward to the goal.
An athlete straining toward the finish line.
“Do not fear, for I am with you.”
live: Prepare for the fast
Plan how you will keep Moonnu Nombu: food, prayer, confession.
Count loss as gain (Philippians 3:8)
Give up one thing this week for the sake of Christ.
Pray for vocations
Pray daily for young people whom Christ is calling.
Unity Octave
Pray each day for the unity of all Christians.
fathers: St John Chrysostom (in substance)
Paul does not say he has attained, but that he presses on; the one who thinks he has arrived stops running.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
The Ninevites fasted for three days and the threatened city was saved; let us also turn, and the gate of mercy will open.
magis: God's election of a people for a mission.
Fasting, prayer and almsgiving in conversion.
Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches, can. 882
Days of fasting and penance in the Eastern Churches.
saints: 18–20 Jan: Moonnu Nombu. 18–25 Jan: Church Unity Octave. 20 Jan: St Sebastian. 22 Jan: Third Friday of Denha, the Evangelists.
2027-01-17.prayer: Lord our God, you chose Joshua, Israel and the Twelve, and you have called us in your Son. Make us strong and bold, free from fear, ready to count all things loss for the surpassing value of knowing Christ. As we begin the fast of the Ninevites, turn our hearts to you, and let us press on toward the prize of your heavenly call. Glory to you, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-24.title: Fourth Sunday of Denha
2027-01-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Jacob beside the well of Laban
2027-01-24.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave concludes tomorrow, the Conversion of St Paul.
2027-01-24.verse: but those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty. The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.”
theo: Denha is the season of Christ's manifestation, and today he is revealed beside a well. In Genesis Jacob, a fugitive far from home, comes to a well, rolls away the stone, waters Rachel's flock, “kissed Rachel, and wept aloud.” A well in the Bible is a place of meeting and of new beginnings. The second reading tells how the Samaritans came to be: foreigners settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king, who learned something of the LORD but mixed his worship with their own gods. By Jesus' time Jews and Samaritans did not share even a drinking vessel.

So when Jesus, tired from the journey, sits by Jacob's well at noon and says to a Samaritan woman, “Give me a drink”, he crosses every barrier: of race, of religion, of gender, of reputation. He offers her “living water”, and she misunderstands, thinking of the well. “Everyone who drinks of this water will be thirsty again, but those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty.” He reads her life with truth and without contempt. She speaks of the place of worship; he answers that “God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.” When she says the Messiah is coming, Jesus makes one of the clearest revelations in the Gospel: “I am he, the one who is speaking to you.”

Hebrews urges believers to move beyond the beginnings of faith toward maturity, and not to “become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.” The woman left her water jar and ran to tell the town. Denha asks us the same: have we drunk the living water, and are we telling others? The Church is meant to be a well where every thirsty person can meet Christ.
conn: Wells of meeting.
Isaac's servant met Rebekah at a well (Genesis 24), Jacob met Rachel (Genesis 29), Moses met Zipporah (Exodus 2). Jesus meets the Samaritan woman at Jacob's well.
Samaritans.
Descendants of the northern Israelites mixed with settlers brought by Assyria (2 Kings 17). They worshipped on Mount Gerizim and accepted only the five books of Moses.
Noon.
The sixth hour, the heat of the day; perhaps the woman came when no one else would see her. It is also the hour of Jesus' condemnation (John 19:14).
Living water.
Running spring water, in contrast to still cistern water; in John it signifies the Holy Spirit (John 7:38–39).
“I am he”.
Greek ego eimi, echoing the divine name revealed to Moses (Exodus 3:14).
Five husbands.
Some Fathers saw an allusion to the five peoples and their gods in 2 Kings 17; Jesus offers the true worship.
altar: The living water first given in Baptism is renewed at every Qurbana, where the Spirit is invoked in the epiclesis.
Like the woman, we receive Christ and then are sent to the town: “Go in peace.”
outline: Ask: what are you thirsty for today?
The Messiah revealed; leave the jar and tell others.
An empty water jar left by the well.
“A spring of water gushing up to eternal life.”
live: Cross a barrier
Speak kindly to someone your community avoids.
Drink the living water
Make time for quiet prayer to the Holy Spirit each day this week.
Leave your jar
Let go of one thing you rely on instead of God.
Tell the town
Share with one person what Christ means to you.
fathers: St Ephrem the Syrian
Our Lord came to the spring as a hunter; he asked for water so that he might give water; he asked as one thirsting so that he might quench thirst.
St Augustine
He who asked for a drink was thirsting for her faith.
magis: Prayer as the meeting of God's thirst and ours, with the Samaritan woman.
Living water: symbol of the Spirit; worship in spirit and truth.
Worship in spirit and truth is not tied to one place.
Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches, can. 584
The Church's missionary duty to proclaim the Gospel to all.
saints: 25 Jan: Conversion of St Paul; Unity Octave ends. 26 Jan: Republic Day; Sts Timothy and Titus. 28 Jan: St Thomas Aquinas. 29 Jan: Fourth Friday of Denha, St Stephen. 31 Jan: Fifth Sunday of Denha; St John Bosco.
2027-01-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, at Jacob's well you asked for a drink and offered living water. Satisfy our thirst with your Holy Spirit, teach us to worship in spirit and truth, and make us, like the Samaritan woman, eager to leave our jars and bring others to you. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-31.title: Fifth Sunday of Denha
2027-01-31.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness
Redemption and forgiveness through the Son
The Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins
2027-01-31.alt: Season of Denha. St John Bosco: Philippians 4:4–9; Matthew 18:1–5.
2027-01-31.verse: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
theo: Today's readings are a single long meditation on forgiveness. In Leviticus, when the whole congregation sins unknowingly, a bull is offered, its blood sprinkled before the veil, and “the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.” Israel learned that sin is serious and that forgiveness is costly. In exile Daniel reads Jeremiah, fasts in sackcloth, and confesses for all the people: “we have sinned and done wrong… To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him.” Forgiveness is not owed; it belongs to God's mercy.

Then in Capernaum the house is so crowded that four friends dig through the roof and lower a paralysed man on his mat in front of Jesus. “When Jesus saw their faith”, the faith of the friends, “he said to the paralytic, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’” The scribes are right in their premise: “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” They are wrong in their conclusion. Jesus answers: “so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”, and the man stands up, takes his mat and walks out before them all. The God of the sin offering and of Daniel's prayer is present in person.

Paul tells the Colossians what this means: the Father “has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins. He is the image of the invisible God.” In Denha Christ is revealed as the one who forgives. That authority he gave to his Church: “If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them.” Every confession is Capernaum again. And like the four friends, we are called to carry to Christ those who cannot come by themselves. Today we also honour St John Bosco, who carried countless young people to Christ.
conn: The sin offering.
Leviticus 4 distinguishes sins of the priest, the congregation, a leader and an individual; each requires blood, the sign of life given (Leviticus 17:11).
Daniel's prayer.
A model of communal confession: he says “we” not “they” (Daniel 9:5).
Through the roof.
Palestinian roofs were made of beams, branches and packed clay; the friends literally dug through.
Their faith.
Jesus responds to the faith of the friends; intercession matters (CCC 2634–2636).
Son of Man.
Daniel's title (Daniel 7:13) for the one given everlasting dominion; Jesus uses it of himself.
The sacrament.
Christ gave the apostles and their successors the power to forgive sins (John 20:22–23; CCC 1441–1442).
altar: At the Qurbana we pray for the forgiveness of sins, and receive the Body and Blood given “for the forgiveness of sins” (Matthew 26:28).
The Lamb once sacrificed ends all sin offerings; his one sacrifice is made present on our altar.
outline: Ask: who would carry you to Jesus if you could not walk?
A man walking out with his mat on his shoulder.

Confess as “we” (Daniel 9:5)

Encourage a young person in faith or study.

He first heals the soul, then the body, to show which is the greater sickness.
St Ephrem the Syrian (in substance)
The friends opened the roof, and the Lord opened the man's soul; what they lowered on a mat, he raised by his word.

Christ the physician of souls and bodies, in the sacraments of healing.

2027-01-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, image of the invisible God, you have authority on earth to forgive sins. Forgive us, raise us up from all that paralyses us, and make us like the four friends who carried the sick to you. Through the prayers of St John Bosco, help us bring the young to you. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-02.title: First Saturday of Nativity
2027-01-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: You have been enriched in him in speech and knowledge
Anna speaks of the child; Jesus grows in wisdom
2027-01-02.verse: The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favor of God was upon him.
theo: Luke ends the story of the Presentation with an old woman: Anna, a prophet, widowed after seven years of marriage and now eighty-four. “She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.” At the very moment the Holy Family is in the Temple, she comes, praises God, “and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.” A lifetime of hidden prayer ends in joyful witness.

Then the family returns to Nazareth, where “the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom.” Paul thanks God that the Corinthians “have been enriched in him, in speech and knowledge of every kind”, so that they are “not lacking in any spiritual gift” as they wait for the Lord. God is faithful; he gives his people what they need to grow. Anna in old age and the Child in his youth both show that every stage of life can be full of God.
outline: Ask: who is an elderly person whose prayer has carried your family?
She speaks to all who wait.
Nazareth and the gifts of grace.
“The favor of God was upon him.”
live: Honour the praying elders
Thank a grandparent or elderly parishioner for their prayers.
Grow in wisdom (Luke 2:40)
Choose one spiritual book to read slowly this year.
2027-01-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you grew in wisdom at Nazareth, and Anna proclaimed you to all who waited. Make me faithful in prayer like her, and help me to grow in your grace all through this year. Amen.
altar: Anna spent her life in the Temple. In the Holy Qurbana we too stand before the Lord; our faithful presence, Sunday after Sunday, becomes witness.

2027-01-04.title: Second Monday of Nativity
2027-01-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Whatever is born of God conquers the world
The Son does what he sees the Father doing
2027-01-04.verse: for whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.
theo: In these last days of Nativity the Church asks who the Child is. Jesus answers in the Gospel: “the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.” This is not weakness but perfect unity. The Son gives life as the Father gives life, and judges as the Father has entrusted to him, “so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.” The Child of Bethlehem is worthy of the same worship as the Father.

St John draws out what this means for believers: “Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God.” Faith is a new birth. And this new birth is strong: “whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.” The world with its fears, temptations and pressures does not have the last word over a child of God.
outline: Ask: what in the world around you seems stronger than your faith?
Point 2 · The Son and the Father
One in work, one in honour.
The victory that overcomes the world.
“This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.”
live: Honour the Son (John 5:23)
Make a slow, reverent Sign of the Cross each time you pray today.
Overcome by faith (1 John 5:4)
Face one fear today with an act of faith: Jesus, I trust in you.
2027-01-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal Son of the Father, you do the works of the Father and give life to whom you will. I believe that you are the Christ; let this faith be my victory over every fear and temptation. Glory to you with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we give glory to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit together. The Son receives the same honour as the Father.

2027-01-05.title: Second Tuesday of Nativity · Eve of Denha
2027-01-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Moses faithful as a servant, Christ as a son
2027-01-05.alt: Season of Nativity. Readings of the Second Set, mapped from the official calendar. Tonight many families keep the Denha customs: lamps on plantain stems (pindikuthi) and the night bath recalling the Jordan (rakkuli).
2027-01-05.verse: Christ, however, was faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.
theo: On the eve of Denha the Church sets two great figures side by side. Hebrews honours Moses: he “was faithful in all God's house as a servant.” But Jesus is greater, “faithful over God's house as a son”, as the builder is greater than the house. And then a surprise: “we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.” The house of God is not only a building; it is the people who keep faith.

In the Gospel the priests and Levites question John at the Jordan. He refuses every great title: he is not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the prophet. He is a voice, and he baptises only with water: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Tomorrow that unknown one will come down into the Jordan and be revealed by the Father's voice and the Spirit. Our ancestors in Kerala kept this night with lights on plantain stems, crying “El Paiya”, God is light, and with a bath in river or pond recalling the Jordan. Tonight let us prepare our hearts to see him.
outline: Ask: what do the lights and the bath of the Denha eve mean?
Point 3 · One whom you do not know
live: Keep the Denha eve
Light a lamp at home tonight and pray: Christ, light of the world, shine on our family.
Hold firm (Hebrews 3:6)
Renew one good resolution you have let slip.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, faithful Son over God's house, John prepared your way at the Jordan. On this holy night make our home your house, and let us hold firm in hope until we see your glory. Amen.
altar: The Church gathered for the Holy Qurbana is God's house built of living stones. Christ is its faithful Son and builder.

2027-01-07.title: First Thursday of Denha
2027-01-07.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Christ is proclaimed in every way
He must increase, but I must decrease
2027-01-07.verse: What does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether out of false motives or true; and in that I rejoice.
theo: The day after Denha the Church listens to two men who were glad when Christ was made known, whatever it cost them. Paul writes from prison, yet his letter is full of joy: “what has happened to me has actually helped to spread the gospel.” His chains have become a sermon to the imperial guard, and other believers have grown bolder. Some preach Christ out of rivalry, hoping to hurt Paul; he does not mind: “Christ is proclaimed in every way… and in that I rejoice.”

John the Baptist shows the same freedom when his disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” The friend of the bridegroom rejoices at the bridegroom's voice. In the season of Denha, when Christ is manifested to the world, the Church asks us to check our hearts: do we rejoice when Christ is known, even through others, even at our expense?
outline: Ask: how do you react when someone else does the good work you hoped to do?
John's joy as the bridegroom's friend.
“Christ is proclaimed in every way… and in that I rejoice.”
live: Offer your chains (Philippians 1:12)
Offer one hardship today for the spread of the Gospel.
Rejoice in others' good (John 3:29)
Congratulate sincerely someone in the parish whose work is praised.
2027-01-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, manifested at the Jordan, let your name be proclaimed in every way. Free me from envy and rivalry; let me rejoice when you increase, even if I decrease. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana proclaims the death and resurrection of the Lord until he comes. Every Qurbana, in every parish, is Christ proclaimed: we rejoice in all of them.

2027-01-08.title: First Friday of Denha · Commemoration of St John the Baptist
2027-01-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I appoint you over nations, to pluck up and to pull down
James is killed; Peter is freed
The beheading of John the Baptist
2027-01-08.alt: Season of Denha. The Third Qudasha is used today.
2027-01-08.verse: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the LORD.
theo: On the Fridays of Denha the Church honours the great witnesses who made Christ known. The first is John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open over Jesus at the Jordan. Today's readings form a gallery of prophetic courage. Nathan goes to King David after his adultery and murder and, through a simple story, leads him to condemn himself; then he says: “You are the man!” Jeremiah, young and afraid, is told: “Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you.”

John paid the price of this courage. He told Herod plainly, “It is not lawful for you to have her.” Herod imprisoned him, and at a drunken birthday banquet, to keep a foolish oath, had him beheaded. In Acts, King Herod Agrippa kills James with the sword and arrests Peter; “the church prayed fervently to God for him”, and an angel leads Peter out. Some witnesses are freed, some are killed; all are held by God. In a world where power often silences conscience, the Baptist's head on a platter is a question to every Christian: will I speak the truth with love, whatever it costs?
outline: Ask: when was the last time you said a hard truth with love?
Nathan's courage leads David to repentance.
Jeremiah and John, consecrated before birth.
“I am with you to deliver you.”
live: Speak the truth with love
Correct one wrong gently and honestly, instead of keeping silent.
Pray for the persecuted (Acts 12:5)
Pray today for Christians imprisoned or threatened for their faith.
2027-01-08.prayer: O God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way of your Son and to bear witness to the truth even to death. Give us courage like Nathan, Jeremiah and John, to speak the truth with love, and keep your persecuted Church in your hand. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today. At the altar we unite ourselves with the witnesses who offered their lives with Christ.

2027-01-09.title: First Saturday of Denha
2027-01-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Holy is the Lord God the Almighty
Are you the one who is to come?
2027-01-09.verse: And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them.
theo: From prison John the Baptist sends two disciples to ask Jesus: “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?” Even the great witness has a moment of darkness. Perhaps he expected a Messiah of fire and judgement. Jesus does not argue. He shows what he is doing: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear good news. These are the signs Isaiah promised (Isaiah 35:5–6; 61:1). And he adds: “blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.”

The epistle opens a door in heaven. John the seer sees a throne, a rainbow, twenty-four elders and four living creatures who “Day and night without ceasing… sing, ‘Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come.’” The Church on earth joins this song in every Qurbana. When we doubt, as John did in prison, we look at the works of Christ among the poor and we lift our eyes to the throne: he is the one who is to come.
outline: Ask: have you ever doubted, even after years of faith?
Doubt in the dark of prison.
Jesus answers with deeds of mercy.
“Blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.”
live: Bring your doubts to Jesus
Tell Jesus honestly any doubt you carry, as John did.
Be a sign (Luke 7:22)
Do one work of mercy today so that someone sees Christ at work.
2027-01-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, you answered John's doubt with deeds of mercy. When I am in darkness, show me your works, lift my eyes to your throne, and let me join the angels' song: Holy, holy, holy. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we sing “Holy, holy, holy” with the angels and the living creatures. Heaven's worship and ours are one.

2027-01-11.title: Second Monday of Denha
2027-01-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Christ is head over all things
The one who comes from above is above all
2027-01-11.verse: And he has put all things under his feet and has made him the head over all things for the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.
theo: Paul prays for the Ephesians “so that, with the eyes of your heart enlightened, you may know what is the hope to which he has called you.” Faith has eyes: it sees what the world cannot see. And what does it see? The immeasurable power of God at work in raising Christ from the dead and seating him at his right hand, “far above all rule and authority”. God has made Christ “the head over all things for the church, which is his body”. The Church is not a human club; she is the Body of the risen Lord.

John the Baptist says the same in the Gospel: “The one who comes from above is above all… The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life.” In Denha we contemplate Christ revealed: not one teacher among many, but the Lord above all. The practical question is simple: is Christ really above all in my life, above my plans, my fears, my money, my time?
outline: Ask: what is at the top of your list of priorities?
Faith sees the hope of our calling.
The risen Christ and his Body.
The Father has placed all in his hands.
“The one who comes from above is above all.”
live: Pray for enlightened eyes (Ephesians 1:18)
Ask the Holy Spirit each morning to open the eyes of your heart.
Put Christ first
Give Christ the first moment of your day and the first part of your income.
2027-01-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, risen and seated at the Father's right hand, you are head over all things. Enlighten the eyes of my heart, let me see the hope of my calling, and be truly first in my life. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is offered for the whole Church, the Body of Christ. Here the Head and the members are united.

2027-01-12.title: Second Tuesday of Denha
2027-01-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The Son of God was revealed to destroy the works of the devil
The unclean spirit confesses the Holy One of God
2027-01-12.verse: See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are. The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him.
theo: St John begins with wonder: “See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are.” This is not a title only; it is a new reality given in Baptism. And it has a purpose: “The Son of God was revealed for this purpose, to destroy the works of the devil.” Denha, the revelation of the Son, is God's campaign against evil. Those born of God do not make sin their way of life.

Mark shows the campaign beginning. In the synagogue of Capernaum a man with an unclean spirit cries out: “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” The demons recognise him before the people do. Jesus rebukes the spirit: “Be silent, and come out of him!” and the man is freed. Christ has come to set us free; our part is to live as the children we are.
outline: Ask: what does it mean to you to be a child of God?
Point 2 · To destroy the works of the devil
The purpose of the Son's revelation.
“See what love the Father has given us.”
live: Live as a child of God (1 John 3:1)
Each time you are tempted today, say: I am a child of God.
Pray for deliverance
Pray the St Michael prayer for those oppressed by evil.
2027-01-12.prayer: Father, see what love you have given us: we are your children. Your Son was revealed to destroy the works of the devil. Free us from every evil, and let us live as your children in holiness and love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Before Communion we pray, “deliver us from evil.” In the Holy Qurbana Christ's victory over the evil one becomes ours.

2027-01-13.title: Second Wednesday of Denha
2027-01-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Blessed are those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb
The first sign at Cana: Jesus revealed his glory
2027-01-13.verse: Jesus did this, the first of his signs, in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.
theo: The ancient Church celebrated three manifestations together: the Magi, the Baptism in the Jordan and the wedding at Cana. Today, in the season of Denha, we hear of Cana. At a village wedding the wine runs out, a disaster for the family's honour. Mary notices and says simply: “They have no wine.” Then she tells the servants: “Do whatever he tells you.” Six stone jars for purification are filled with water, and the water becomes the best wine. John says: “Jesus did this, the first of his signs… and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.”

Revelation shows where Cana points: “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” The wedding at Cana is a sign of the great wedding between Christ and his Church, and of the Eucharist where his blood becomes our wine of joy. Mary's words are the best advice ever given: “Do whatever he tells you.” When our lives run out of wine, of joy, love or strength, let us tell Jesus through Mary, and do what he says.
outline: Ask: when has your “wine” run out?
Point 2 · Do whatever he tells you
Point 3 · The marriage supper of the Lamb
Cana points to the Eucharist and heaven.
live: Tell Mary your need (John 2:3)
Pray one decade of the Rosary today for a family whose wine has run out.
Obey one word (John 2:5)
Do one thing Jesus asks of you that you have been delaying.
2027-01-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, at Cana you revealed your glory and turned water into wine. Through the prayers of your Mother, fill what is empty in our homes, and help us do whatever you tell us, until we sit at the marriage supper of the Lamb. Amen.
altar: The wine of Cana points to the cup of the Holy Qurbana. Here the Bridegroom gives his own blood to his bride, the Church.

2027-01-14.title: Second Thursday of Denha · St Devasahayam
2027-01-14.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit
Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up
2027-01-14.alt: Season of Denha. St Devasahayam, martyr: Romans 9:30–33; John 10:31–39.
2027-01-14.verse: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God, and that you are not your own? For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.
theo: After Cana, John shows Jesus in the Temple of Jerusalem at Passover. He makes a whip of cords, drives out the sellers and overturns the tables: “Stop making my Father's house a marketplace!” The disciples remember the psalm: “Zeal for your house will consume me.” Asked for a sign, Jesus says: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” John explains: “he was speaking of the temple of his body.” The true meeting place of God and humanity is now the body of Jesus, crucified and risen.

Paul draws the conclusion for us: “your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you… you are not your own. For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.” Christian chastity, sobriety and care for health are not rules imposed from outside; they are reverence for a temple. Today the Church in India honours St Devasahayam, who after his Baptism refused to treat anyone as untouchable and gave his body in martyrdom. In him the temple of the body became a living offering.
outline: Ask: how do we behave inside a church? Why?
Point 1 · Zeal for the Father's house
Point 2 · The temple of his body
Destroyed and raised in three days.
live: Reverence in church (John 2:16)
Arrive early for Qurbana, keep silence, and switch off your phone.
Honour your body (1 Corinthians 6:19)
Give up one habit that harms your body: excess alcohol, tobacco, junk viewing.
2027-01-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, zeal for your Father's house consumed you, and your body became the true temple, destroyed and raised for us. Cleanse the temple of my body and heart, and through the prayers of St Devasahayam make my life a living offering. Amen.
altar: The church building is God's house; the Body of Christ on the altar is the true Temple; and we who receive him become temples of the Spirit.

2027-01-15.title: Second Friday of Denha · Commemoration of Sts Peter and Paul, the Apostles
2027-01-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: You shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation
Called through grace to proclaim the Son
Simon, do you love me? Feed my sheep
2027-01-15.verse: When they had finished breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my lambs.”
theo: On the second Friday of Denha the Church honours the two pillars who made Christ known to the world: Peter and Paul. Peter had denied Jesus three times by a charcoal fire. Now, by another charcoal fire at the lake, the risen Lord asks him three times: “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Each answer is followed by a mission: feed my lambs, tend my sheep, feed my sheep. Jesus does not choose a perfect man; he chooses a forgiven one, and builds his flock on love. Then he foretells that Peter too will be led where he does not wish to go: martyrdom in Rome.

Paul tells his own story in Galatians: once he “was violently persecuting the church of God”, but God, “who had set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace, was pleased to reveal his Son to me, so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles.” In Acts, Peter preaches to the Gentile household of Cornelius: “God shows no partiality.” Two very different men, one denier and one persecutor, both transformed by grace, both martyred in Rome. Through them Israel's calling to be “a priestly kingdom and a holy nation” reaches all nations, including us.
outline: Ask: has God ever used your failure for good?
Israel's call fulfilled in the Church.
“Lord, you know that I love you.”
live: Answer Jesus' question (John 21:15)
Tell Jesus today in your own words: Lord, you know that I love you.
Pray for the Pope
Pray for the Successor of Peter and for our Major Archbishop.
2027-01-15.prayer: Lord Jesus, you forgave Peter and called Paul by grace, and made them pillars of your Church. Through their prayers, make us love you above all, feed your flock, and proclaim you to all nations. Bless our Holy Father the Pope and all our shepherds. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is offered in communion with the Pope, the Successor of Peter, and with our bishops. The love Jesus asked of Peter is the love we bring to the altar.

2027-01-16.title: Second Saturday of Denha
2027-01-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: He emptied himself, taking the form of a slave
Learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart
2027-01-16.verse: Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
theo: Jesus prays aloud: “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants.” The revelation celebrated in Denha is received not by the proud but by the little. Then he turns to us with the most tender invitation in the Gospels: “Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest… learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart.”

Paul shows how deep this humility goes. “Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be exploited, but emptied himself, taking the form of a slave.” He humbled himself to death on a cross, and therefore God exalted him. At the end of this week of Denha, the revealed Lord shows us his heart: gentle and humble. His yoke is not a heavy law but a shared harness with him, and in it we find rest.
outline: Ask: what burden are you carrying this week?
“I am gentle and humble in heart.”
live: Bring your burden (Matthew 11:28)
Sit before Jesus for five minutes and name your heaviest burden.
Learn humility (Philippians 2:5)
Do one humble service today without being seen.
2027-01-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, you emptied yourself for us. Reveal the Father to me as to a little child, take my burden, and let me learn from you and find rest for my soul. Amen.
altar: The Son who emptied himself on the Cross empties himself again into the humble form of bread. Come to him and find rest.

I came to call not the righteous but sinners
2027-01-18.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). Church Unity Octave begins (Ephesians 4:1–6; John 17:6–11).
2027-01-18.verse: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity that he had said he would bring upon them; and he did not do it.
theo: Today begins the Three Days' Fast, the fast of the Ninevites. Jonah walks into the great city with a short, terrible message: “Forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!” And something astonishing happens: “the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.” Even the king leaves his throne and sits in ashes. “When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind.” The East Syriac Church has kept this fast since the sixth century, when a plague was stopped after the people fasted and prayed; in Kerala, Kuravilangad and many parishes still draw great crowds.

Moses promises the same mercy: if you “return to the LORD your God… the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you.” In the Gospel Jesus calls Matthew, a tax collector, and eats with sinners. To the critics he says: “Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.” Our fast is not a show of strength but an opening to mercy. Jude blesses God “who is able to keep you from falling”. Today the Unity Octave also begins: may our conversion help heal the divisions among Christians.

Great and small fast and turn.

2027-01-18.prayer: Merciful God, when Nineveh fasted and turned from evil, you relented. Look on us in these three days of fasting; turn our hearts, forgive our sins, and keep us from falling. Make all Christians one in your mercy. Amen.
altar: During the fast the Holy Qurbana is our true food. The mercy that saved Nineveh is given to us at the altar.

2027-01-19.title: Third Tuesday of Denha · Second Day of the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Confess your sins to one another
The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world
2027-01-19.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-19.verse: The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and declared, “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
theo: On the second day of the fast the readings teach us to confess. Solomon, dedicating the Temple, prays that when the people sin and then turn, “acknowledge your name, pray and plead with you in this house”, God will “hear from heaven, and forgive.” Baruch puts words of confession on the lips of exiles: “The Lord our God is in the right, but there is open shame on us today.” True confession does not blame God or others; it says: we have sinned.

James gives the Church's practice: “Are any among you sick? They should call for the elders of the church… Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed.” Here the Church has always seen the sacraments of Anointing and Reconciliation. And the Baptist shows us where sin is taken away: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!” Our fasting is not what removes sin; the Lamb does. The fast prepares us to bring our sins to him in confession.
outline: Ask: why is it so hard to say “I was wrong”?
James and the sacraments of healing.
He takes away the sin of the world.
“Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!”

Pray for and gently reach out to someone who has left the Church.
2027-01-19.prayer: Lamb of God, who take away the sin of the world, have mercy on us. On this second day of the fast, give us the humility to confess our sins and the joy of your forgiveness. Hear us from heaven and heal us. Amen.
altar: Before Communion we pray to the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world. The fast leads us to the Lamb.

2027-01-20.title: Third Wednesday of Denha · Third Day of the Three Days' Fast · St Sebastian
2027-01-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The love of Jacob for Rachel
Return, O Israel; I will love them freely
Love covers a multitude of sins
2027-01-20.alt: Season of Denha. Three Days' Fast (Moonnu Nombu, the Rogation of the Ninevites). St Sebastian, martyr, and the name day of Mar Sebastian Vadakkel, Mar Sebastian Adayanthrath, Mar Sebastian Vaniyapurackal and Mar Sebastian Pozholiparampil. The Third Qudasha (Anaphora of Mar Nestorius) is used today. Readings for St Sebastian: Deuteronomy 32:37–43; Isaiah 49:1–4; 2 Timothy 2:1–5; Matthew 10:24–33.
2027-01-20.verse: Therefore, I tell you, her sins, which were many, have been forgiven; hence she has shown great love. But the one to whom little is forgiven, loves little.”
theo: On the last day of the fast, the readings speak of love. Jacob serves seven years for Rachel, “and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her.” Hosea, after many warnings, ends with God's tender promise: “Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God… I will heal their disloyalty; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned from them.” The goal of all fasting is not hunger but love restored.

In the Gospel a woman known as a sinner enters Simon the Pharisee's house, weeps at Jesus' feet, dries them with her hair and anoints them. Simon judges her; Jesus defends her: “her sins, which were many, have been forgiven; hence she has shown great love.” Peter's letter says: “Above all, maintain constant love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins.” Today we also honour St Sebastian, much loved in Kerala, and pray for our bishops who bear his name. He loved Christ more than life; the forgiven woman loved Christ more than her reputation. Let our fast end in that kind of love.

2027-01-20.prayer: Lord Jesus, you forgave the woman who loved much and defended her before her accusers. As our fast ends, heal our disloyalty, fill us with love that covers many sins, and through the prayers of St Sebastian make us brave in faith. Amen.
altar: The woman anointed Jesus' feet with love; we come to the Holy Qurbana to receive his love and return it.

2027-01-21.title: Third Thursday of Denha · Thursday after the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-21.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked
Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity?
No greater joy than to hear that my children walk in the truth
Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents
2027-01-21.alt: Season of Denha. Thanksgiving after the Three Days' Fast. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-21.verse: Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
theo: The fast is over, and the Church celebrates the joy of God who forgives. Ezekiel hears God swear: “As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live.” Micah sings: “Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity…? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency… You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.” After three days of turning, we hear God's answer: mercy.

In the Gospel tax collectors and sinners come near to Jesus, and the Pharisees grumble. Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one lost sheep, and of a woman who sweeps her house to find one lost coin. When they find them, they call their neighbours: “Rejoice with me.” “Just so… there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.” John the Elder writes: “I have no greater joy than this, to hear that my children are walking in the truth.” The fruit of the fast is joy: God's joy over us, and our joy in walking in his truth.

Micah's God who delights in mercy.
“Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.”

2027-01-21.prayer: God of mercy, you take no pleasure in the death of sinners and you cast our sins into the depths of the sea. Thank you for the grace of these days of fasting. Let us share heaven's joy over every sinner who returns, and walk always in your truth. Amen.
altar: Each Qurbana is a feast of the found: we were lost, and the Shepherd carries us home on his shoulders to his table.

2027-01-22.title: Third Friday of Denha · Commemoration of the Evangelists
2027-01-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The seed is the word of God
2027-01-22.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-22.verse: But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
theo: On the third Friday of Denha the Church honours the four Evangelists: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, through whom Christ is made known to the whole world. The readings use rich symbols. In Eden “a river flows out… and from there it divides and becomes four branches”, watering the earth: the Fathers saw in the four rivers the four Gospels flowing from Christ to every land. Ezekiel and Revelation describe four living creatures around God's throne, with the faces of a human being, a lion, an ox and an eagle; tradition linked them to Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

The Gospel is the parable of the sower: “The seed is the word of God.” Some falls on the path, some on rock, some among thorns. “But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.” The Evangelists wrote so that the seed could reach us. The question for us is the soil: do we let the Gospel take root, or do worries and pleasures choke it?
outline: Ask: which Gospel is your favourite, and why?
The Gospel flows to every land.
Hold the word fast and bear fruit.
“Hold it fast in an honest and good heart.”

2027-01-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, through the four Evangelists your Gospel has flowed like rivers to the ends of the earth. Make my heart good soil, honest and patient, so that your word may bear fruit in me. Amen.
altar: The Gospel book is carried in honour in the Holy Qurbana; Christ speaks when it is read. Then he feeds us with himself.

2027-01-23.title: Third Saturday of Denha
2027-01-23.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved
2027-01-23.alt: Season of Denha. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-23.verse: because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
theo: Paul tells the Romans that salvation is not far away, as if we had to climb to heaven or descend into the abyss to find it: “The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart.” Faith is simple and total: “if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.” And it is for everyone: “there is no distinction between Jew and Greek… Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”

Mark shows what calling on the Lord looks like. A leper, excluded from every town, comes to Jesus, kneels and begs: “If you choose, you can make me clean.” Jesus is moved with pity, touches him and heals him. The leper did what Paul describes: he called on the Lord with his lips, trusting with his heart. Salvation is near to anyone who calls, however far they feel from God. This is the good news of Denha for all peoples.

2027-01-25.title: Fourth Monday of Denha · Conversion of Saint Paul
2027-01-25.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God calls Moses from the burning bush
He appeared also to me, as to one untimely born
2027-01-25.alt: Season of Denha. Conversion of St Paul. The Church Unity Octave concludes. Weekday readings of the day: 2 Corinthians 5:17–21; John 4:27–30, 39–42.
2027-01-25.verse: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me has not been in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them—though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me.
theo: Today's readings set two great calls side by side. Moses, a fugitive shepherd in the desert, sees a bush that burns and is not consumed, and hears his name: “Moses, Moses!” God reveals himself: “I AM WHO I AM.” Saul, a zealous persecutor on the road, is thrown to the ground by a light from heaven and hears his name: “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” He asks, “Who are you, Lord?” and hears: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.” The God of the burning bush has a human face and a name, and he identifies himself with his suffering Church.

Saul is led blind into Damascus. Ananias, frightened but obedient, lays hands on him; “something like scales fell from his eyes, and his sight was restored.” He is baptized, and “immediately he began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, saying, ‘He is the Son of God.’” Years later Paul looks back with humility: Christ appeared to Cephas, to the Twelve, to more than five hundred, to James, “Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. For I am the least of the apostles.” And then the great sentence: “by the grace of God I am what I am.”

The Gospel explains this grace. The owner of the vineyard hires workers at dawn, at nine, at noon, at three, and even at five o'clock, and pays them all the same. Those hired first grumble. He answers: “Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or are you envious because I am generous?” Paul was hired at the eleventh hour, and received the full wage of grace. None of us earns salvation; all of us receive it. This is the good news for every latecomer, and the end of all envy in the Church.
conn: Two calls by name.
“Moses, Moses” (Exodus 3:4) and “Saul, Saul” (Acts 9:4): the double name marks a decisive call.
I AM.
The divine name revealed at the bush is echoed in Jesus' words, “I am Jesus” (Acts 9:5).
Scales from the eyes.
A sign of baptismal enlightenment; the early Church called Baptism “illumination”.
Untimely born.
Paul's image for his late and unexpected call; grace overturns ordinary timing.
The eleventh hour.
Workers hired at five o'clock receive a full day's wage; the Fathers saw here the Gentiles and late converts.
Unity Octave.
Ends today: the apostle who once divided now unites.
altar: Paul's sight was restored, then he was baptized and ate (Acts 9:18–19). Baptism leads to the table of the Qurbana.
At the altar no one is paid by merit; all receive the same Lord, by grace.

2027-01-26.title: Fourth Tuesday of Denha · Republic Day of India
2027-01-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Those who gladly accepted the word
Whoever is from God hears the words of God
2027-01-26.alt: Season of Denha. Republic Day of India. Sts Timothy and Titus: 2 Samuel 22:2–4; Wisdom 7:28–8:3; 1 Timothy 6:11–16; Matthew 16:24–27.
2027-01-26.verse: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, for in spite of persecution you received the word with joy inspired by the Holy Spirit,
theo: Paul's earliest letter begins with thanksgiving for a young Church in Thessalonica: “remembering before our God and Father your work of faith and labor of love and steadfastness of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.” Faith that works, love that labours, hope that endures: this is the whole Christian life in one line. The Gospel came to them “not in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction”, and they received it with joy even under persecution. Timothy, whom the Church honours today with Titus, was sent back to this very community to strengthen it.

In the Gospel Jesus argues with those who claim Abraham as their father but reject the truth he brings: “Whoever is from God hears the words of God.” Belonging to God is shown by listening to God. On Republic Day, when India remembers the Constitution that came into force in 1950, guaranteeing justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all and the freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion, Christians are asked to be citizens of that same kind: people whose faith works, whose love labours for the common good, whose hope does not give up on the nation. We give thanks for our country, pray for those who govern, and commit ourselves to truth in public life.

Point 2 · The word received with joy

2027-01-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, your word came to Thessalonica in power and in the Holy Spirit. Make our faith active, our love tireless and our hope steadfast. On this Republic Day bless India with justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, and through the prayers of Sts Timothy and Titus make us faithful servants of your Gospel. Amen.

2027-01-27.title: Fourth Wednesday of Denha
2027-01-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Serve the Lord with undivided devotion
Mary has chosen the better part
2027-01-27.verse: there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part, which will not be taken away from her.”
theo: Paul writes to Corinth with a sense of urgency: “the appointed time has grown short… the present form of this world is passing away.” Married or unmarried, buying or mourning, Christians should hold the things of this world lightly. He praises those who give themselves to God in celibacy, so that they may be “holy in body and spirit”, and says his purpose is “to promote good order and unhindered devotion to the Lord.” The Church has always honoured consecrated virginity as a sign of the Kingdom, while also honouring marriage as a true vocation and a sacrament.

In the Gospel Martha welcomes Jesus and is busy with much serving; Mary sits at his feet and listens. Martha complains, and Jesus answers gently: “Martha, Martha, you are worried and distracted by many things; there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part.” Jesus does not despise Martha's service; he corrects her anxiety. Service without listening becomes distraction. The one thing necessary is Christ himself, received in his word. Every vocation, married, consecrated or single, must keep a place at the Lord's feet.
outline: Ask: when did busyness last crowd out prayer for you?

altar: At the Qurbana we sit at the Lord's feet to hear his word, and then he serves us at his table.

2027-01-28.title: Fourth Thursday of Denha · St Thomas Aquinas
2027-01-28.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Jesus is the fulfilment of the promise
I am the resurrection and the life
2027-01-28.alt: Season of Denha. St Thomas Aquinas: 1 Kings 3:5–12; Wisdom 7:7–14; 1 Corinthians 1:18–25; Matthew 5:13–16.
2027-01-28.verse: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
theo: Paul reasons with the Galatians like a lawyer. A will, once ratified, cannot be changed by a later addition. God made a promise to Abraham four hundred and thirty years before the law of Moses, and the law cannot cancel it. And the promise was made “to your offspring”, singular: “that is, to one person, who is Christ.” The whole history of Israel was moving toward one person. In Denha, the season of manifestation, Christ is revealed as the one in whom every promise of God finds its yes.

In the Gospel Jesus arrives at Bethany four days after Lazarus has died. Martha goes out to meet him with grief and faith mixed together: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that God will give you whatever you ask of him.” Jesus reveals himself: “I am the resurrection and the life.” And Martha makes one of the great confessions of the Gospel: “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.” Today the Church honours St Thomas Aquinas, whose great mind served this same faith. He taught that reason can prepare the way, but only faith receives the truth that Christ is the Son of God; and he ended his life in adoration of Christ in the Eucharist, the pledge of our resurrection.
