2027-01-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, offspring of Abraham and fulfilment of every promise, you are the resurrection and the life. Strengthen our faith in sorrow, and through the prayers of St Thomas Aquinas give us minds that seek you and hearts that adore you, until we rise with you. Amen.

2027-01-29.title: Fourth Friday of Denha · Commemoration of St Stephen, Protomartyr
2027-01-29.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-01-29.verse: He replied, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”
theo: On the Fridays of Denha the Church remembers those who manifested Christ by their lives, and today it is Stephen, the first martyr. The readings draw a line of innocent blood. Abel, the righteous brother, is killed by Cain, and God says: “Listen; your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground!” Naboth refuses to sell his ancestral vineyard to King Ahab, is falsely accused by hired witnesses, and is stoned outside the city. Stephen too is accused by false witnesses, his face shining “like the face of an angel”, and is stoned outside Jerusalem.

But Stephen dies differently from Abel and Naboth. He sees “the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!” And as the stones fall he prays: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit… Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” These are almost the words of Jesus on the cross in today's Gospel: “Father, forgive them”, and to the repentant thief, “today you will be with me in Paradise.” Hebrews says the blood of Jesus “speaks a better word than the blood of Abel”: not vengeance, but forgiveness. A young man named Saul held the coats of those who stoned Stephen; Stephen's prayer was answered in Paul. The martyr's forgiveness becomes the seed of the Church.

Point 2 · The face of an angel

2027-01-30.title: Fourth Saturday of Denha
2027-01-30.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-01-30.verse: and be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.
theo: Paul gives the Ephesians a practical rule of life for a community made one in Christ: speak the truth, “for we are members of one another.” “Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and do not make room for the devil.” Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, “but only what is useful for building up.” “Put away from you all bitterness and wrath and anger and wrangling and slander.” And the summit: “be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”

In the Gospel Jesus teaches how to pray: not to be seen by others, but in secret, to the Father who sees in secret; not heaping up empty phrases, for “your Father knows what you need before you ask him.” Then he gives the Our Father, and adds a single commentary, on one line only: “For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” Every time we pray the Lord's Prayer, we ask to be forgiven in the measure we forgive. Saturday, the day before the Lord's Day, is a good day to make peace.

2027-01-01.action: Pray the Jesus Prayer ten times each morning this year.
2027-01-01.question: Do I call on the name of Jesus with faith, or only out of habit?
catechism: The second commandment: the name of the Lord is holy.
kidsaint: He listened to the angel and gave the baby the name Jesus. Lesson: we say Jesus' name with love, never in anger.
2027-01-01.special: Holy Name of Jesus (Circumcision). New Year's Day. Last Friday of Nativity: Divine Motherhood of Mary.
term: Jesus (Yeshua) means “the LORD saves”; the name that is above every name (Philippians 2:9; CCC 432).

family.explain: An angel told Joseph in a dream: Mary will have a son, and you will call him Jesus, because he will save people from their sins.
family.intention: We pray that Jesus will bless every day of this new year for our family.
family.ask: Ask: “Do you know what your name means? Let us find out together.”

illus: An illustration

An old man in a Kuttanad parish could no longer remember his children's names after a stroke. But each evening, when his daughter began the family prayer, he joined in clearly at one word: Ee-sho. The Name he had prayed for eighty years stayed when everything else was fading.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your Name is above every name. We gather in your Name at the start of this new year. Bless us, save us and keep us. Amen.
share: “I have called you by name, you are mine” (Isaiah 43:1). How does it feel to be known by name by God?
“You are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people” (Matthew 1:21). From what do I need Jesus to save me this year?
Every knee should bend at the name of Jesus (Philippians 2:10). How do I honour his Name in my speech?
pm.resp: Jesus, Saviour, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the Name of Jesus to all peoples.
For our families, that this new year may be lived in the Name of Jesus.
For those who take the Lord's Name in vain, that they may come to love it.
For mothers, through the prayers of the Mother of God.
For our group, that we may call on Jesus in every need.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, at the start of this year we place our lives under your holy Name. Save us from sin, guard us from harm, and lead us with Mary your Mother to the Father. Amen.

quick: Those who stay near God shine and learn to listen.
Jesus' first words: I must be in my Father's house.
Our life offered to God is our spiritual worship.
2027-01-03.action: Begin your prayer this week with: Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.
2027-01-03.question: Where do I search for Jesus when I have lost him?
kidsaint: A Kerala priest who started schools next to churches so that every child could learn. Lesson: study well and use your learning to help others.
2027-01-03.special: Second Sunday of Nativity. St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. Denha on Wednesday.
term: Jesus' name for the Temple (Luke 2:49): the place of the Father's presence, and finally his own Body and the Church.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he stayed in the Temple. Mary and Joseph searched for three days and found him listening to the teachers. Jesus went home and obeyed them.
family.intention: We pray for children and parents, that they may understand each other.
family.ask: Ask: “What questions about God would you like to ask?”

illus: An illustration

As Vicar General, St Chavara issued a circular in 1864 asking that every parish church have a school beside it, a 'pallikkoodam'. Many of the first pupils were poor children who had never held a book. Generations later, Kerala's literacy owes much to that simple rule: the Father's house and the school side by side.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were found in your Father's house, listening and asking questions. Speak to us now, for your servants are listening. Amen.
share: “Speak, for your servant is listening” (1 Samuel 3:10). How do I listen to God?
“Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” (Luke 2:49). Where do I find Jesus when I have lost him?
“Present your bodies as a living sacrifice” (Romans 12:1). What can I offer God this week?
pm.resp: Speak, Lord, your servants are listening.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a house where all find the Father.
For parents who worry about their children.
For children and teenagers, that they may grow in wisdom and grace.
For teachers and schools, through the prayers of St Chavara.
For our group, that we may listen to God's word and do it.
pm.close: Heavenly Father, your Son grew in wisdom and favour in the home of Nazareth. Make our homes places of prayer and obedience, and transform us by the renewing of our minds. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed.
God comes down, no longer in terror but in tenderness.
Denha calls us to remember and live our Baptism.
2027-01-06.action: Find out your baptismal date and keep it like a birthday.
2027-01-06.question: Do I live as a beloved child of God?
kidsaint: He baptised Jesus in the river Jordan and saw the Holy Spirit come down like a dove. Lesson: you too were baptised; you are God's beloved child.
2027-01-06.special: Denha: Epiphany and Baptism of the Lord. Day of obligation. Third Qudasha. Beginning of the Season of Denha.
term: Syriac for dawn or manifestation: the revelation of the Holy Trinity at Jesus' Baptism in the Jordan.

family.explain: Jesus went into the river Jordan and John baptised him. The sky opened, the Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and God the Father said: you are my Son, I love you!
family.intention: We pray for all who will be baptised this year.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the day each of us was baptised? Let us find out.”

illus: An illustration

A family in Changanassery keeps a small book with the baptismal date of each child. On that date there is no party, but a candle is lit at dinner and the child renews the baptismal promises. The children say it is their favourite day of the year.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this feast of Denha you went down into the Jordan and the heavens opened. Open heaven over us as we gather, and pour out your Spirit. Amen.
share: The LORD descended upon Sinai in fire (Exodus 19:18). How do I experience God's holiness?
“You are my Son, the Beloved” (Mark 1:11). Do I believe God says this to me?
“Rekindle the gift of God that is within you” (2 Timothy 1:6). What gift of God in me has grown cold?
pm.resp: Christ, our Light, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may shine with the light of the Holy Trinity.
For all baptised Christians, that they may live as children of light.
For catechumens and those preparing for Baptism.
For those who have abandoned the faith received in Baptism.
For our group, that the Spirit may rekindle God's gifts in us.
pm.close: Father, at the Jordan you declared Jesus your beloved Son and anointed him with the Spirit. Keep us faithful to our Baptism, and make our lives shine with your light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's name is I AM: the One who is.
Jesus says: I am from above; believe that I am he.
On the Cross the I AM is revealed in love.
2027-01-10.action: Make an act of faith each morning: Jesus, I believe that you are the Lord.
2027-01-10.question: Do I build my life on the One who is, or on things that pass?
kidsaint: He saw a bush on fire that did not burn up, and God told him his name: I AM. Lesson: God is always there, and he knows your name too.
term: God's name revealed to Moses (Exodus 3:14), YHWH; Jesus applies it to himself (John 8:24, 28) (CCC 211, 590).

family.explain: Moses asked God: what is your name? God said: I AM WHO I AM. Jesus also said: I am. Jesus is God with us.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always trust God who is always there.
family.ask: Ask: “What do you think God's name I AM means?”

illus: An illustration

A boy in Alappuzha, watching the backwaters during a flood, asked his grandfather: everything moves, the water, the boats, the houses; what does not move? The grandfather pointed to the cross on the church tower: He does not move. He said “I AM”. Everything else changes.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the I AM, from above, the Alpha and the Omega. We adore you present among us. Amen.
share: God said “I AM WHO I AM” (Exodus 3:14). What does it mean to me that God simply is?
“You will die in your sins unless you believe that I am he” (John 8:24). How firm is my faith in Jesus?
“When you have lifted up the Son of Man” (John 8:28). What does the Cross reveal to me about God?
pm.resp: You are the Lord; we adore you.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim Jesus as Lord.
For those searching for God, that they may meet the One who is.
For those who have lost faith, that they may look at the Cross.
For our families, that they may build on the rock of faith.
For our group, that we may adore the Lord present among us.
pm.close: Lord God, you revealed your name to Moses and your face in Christ. Keep us faithful to the One who is, lifted up for us, Alpha and Omega. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God chooses people for a mission and goes before them.
Jesus calls those whom he wants.
Paul counts all as loss for Christ and presses on.
2027-01-17.action: Plan how you will keep the Three Days' Fast from tomorrow.
2027-01-17.question: What do I need to count as loss for the sake of Christ?
kidsaint: Moses chose him to lead God's people into the promised land. God told him: be strong and brave, I am with you. Lesson: when you are scared, remember God is with you.
2027-01-17.special: Third Sunday of Denha. Moonnu Nombu and the Church Unity Octave begin tomorrow.
term: The Three Days' Fast of the Ninevites, kept from the Monday to the Wednesday on Monday to Wednesday of the third week before the Great Fast (in 2027, 18–20 January), in memory of Nineveh's repentance (Jonah 3).

family.explain: Jesus went up a mountain and called twelve friends to be with him and to tell others about God.
family.intention: We pray for our family as we begin the Three Days' Fast tomorrow.
family.ask: Ask: “What small sacrifice can each of us make during the three days?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Pala told his parish priest that he had stopped praying because he felt unworthy. The priest read him Isaiah 41: I have chosen you and not cast you off. The young man wrote the verse on his laptop and began to keep the Three Days' Fast with his family. He said: I did not choose God; he chose me first.

pm.open: Lord our God, you have chosen us and not cast us off. Make us strong and bold as we gather, and prepare our hearts for the fast. Amen.
share: “Be strong and bold… it is the LORD who goes before you” (Deuteronomy 31:6, 8). Where do I need courage?
“I have chosen you and not cast you off” (Isaiah 41:9). Do I believe God has chosen me?
“I press on toward the goal” (Philippians 3:14). What lies behind that I must forget?
pm.resp: Lord, you have chosen us; we come.
interc: For the Church, chosen to bring Christ to all peoples.
For vocations to priesthood and religious life.
For a fruitful Three Days' Fast in our families and parishes.
For the unity of Christians.
For our group, that we may press on in faith.
pm.close: Father, you chose us in your Son. Strengthen us to follow him and to press on toward the prize of your heavenly call. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Wells in the Bible are places of meeting and new beginnings.
Jesus crosses every barrier to offer living water.
He reveals himself: I am he, the Messiah.
2027-01-24.action: Speak kindly to someone your community avoids.
2027-01-24.question: What do I keep drinking that never satisfies my thirst?
catechism: God thirsts that we may thirst for him.
Water, symbol of the Holy Spirit.
kidsaint: Tradition calls her St Photina. She met Jesus at a well and ran to tell her whole town about him. Lesson: when you know Jesus, tell your friends!
term: Fresh flowing spring water; in John's Gospel, a sign of the Holy Spirit given by Christ.

family.explain: Jesus was tired and thirsty at a well. He asked a woman for water and then told her he could give her special water, living water, so she would never be thirsty again. That water is God's Spirit!
family.intention: We pray for people who are lonely and left out.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week for someone who is left out?”

illus: An illustration

In a dry village in Palakkad, one family's well never ran dry in summer. They put up a board: Anyone may draw water. Neighbours of every religion came. The grandmother said: Jesus asked a stranger for water. How can we refuse anyone?

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you meet us at the well of our thirst. Give us living water as we gather. Amen.
share: Give me a drink (John 4:7). Whom does Jesus ask me to approach?
Living water (John 4:10). What is my soul thirsty for?
I am he (John 4:26). Do I recognise Jesus in my daily life?
pm.resp: Lord, give us this water.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a well for all who thirst.
For those excluded by race, religion or reputation.
For people of other faiths in our land.
For areas suffering from drought and lack of water.
For our group, that we may tell others about Christ.
pm.close: Father, your Son gives living water. Pour out your Spirit on us and send us to share him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Forgiveness is costly and belongs to God's mercy.
Seeing the friends' faith, Jesus forgave and healed the paralytic.
The Son of Man has authority to forgive sins, and gave it to his Church.
2027-01-31.question: Whom can I carry to Jesus through prayer or help?
catechism: God alone forgives; Christ gives the power to the Church.
kidsaint: He was a priest who loved poor boys who had no home. He gave them school, games and Jesus. Lesson: we can help other children come close to Jesus!
2027-01-31.special: Fifth Sunday of Denha. St John Bosco.
term: The words by which the priest, acting in the person of Christ, forgives sins in the sacrament of Reconciliation.

family.explain: Four friends carried a man who could not walk. The house was full, so they made a hole in the roof and let him down to Jesus! Jesus forgave him and healed him.
family.intention: We pray for someone we know who needs Jesus' help.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we carry to Jesus in our prayers this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Idukki four young men take turns every Sunday to carry an elderly paralysed neighbour down a steep hill to the church for the Qurbana. The parish priest calls them the roof diggers. The old man says: I cannot walk, but I have never missed the Lord, because of my four friends.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you forgive sins and raise the paralysed. Forgive us and make us carriers of others. Amen.
share: The priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven (Leviticus 4:20). Do I take sin seriously?
To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness (Daniel 9:9). Do I trust his mercy?
When Jesus saw their faith (Mark 2:5). Whose faith carried me? Whom can I carry?
pm.resp: Lord, forgive us and raise us up.
interc: For the Church, minister of Christ's forgiveness.
For priests who hear confessions.
For the sick and paralysed and those who care for them.
For young people, through St John Bosco.
For our group, that we may carry one another to Christ.
pm.close: Father, in your Son we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins. Raise us up and send us to bring others to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Anna prayed night and day for a lifetime.
She proclaimed the Child to all who were waiting.
Jesus grew in wisdom, and God enriches us with every gift.
2027-01-02.action: Thank a grandparent or elderly parishioner for their prayers.
2027-01-02.question: Am I faithful in prayer even when nothing seems to happen?

family.explain: Old Anna prayed in the Temple every day. When she saw baby Jesus, she was so happy that she told everyone about him.
family.intention: We pray for grandparents and elderly people who pray for us.
family.ask: Ask: “Who prays for our family? Let us thank them.”

illus: An illustration

In a Thrissur parish an old widow sat in the same corner of the church for forty years, rosary in hand. When she died, the parish priest said at her funeral: most of the vocations from this parish came after she began praying for them. No one had known.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Anna waited for you with fasting and prayer and then spoke of you to everyone. Teach us to pray faithfully and to witness joyfully. Amen.
share: Anna prayed night and day (Luke 2:37). What helps me to pray faithfully?
She spoke of the child to all who were waiting (Luke 2:38). To whom can I speak about Jesus?
The child grew and became strong (Luke 2:40). How have I grown in faith this past year?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us faithful.
interc: For widows and the elderly, that they may know their prayer is precious.
For those who wait for God's answer.
For children and young people, that they may grow in wisdom and grace.
For our parish, that it may be rich in every spiritual gift.
For our group, that we may pray night and day.
pm.close: Lord God, you rewarded Anna's long prayer with the sight of your Son. Keep us faithful in prayer and make us glad witnesses of Jesus. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.
The Son does what the Father does and deserves the same honour.
Our faith is the victory that conquers the world.
2027-01-04.action: Face one fear today with an act of faith.
2027-01-04.question: Do I honour Jesus as I honour the Father?

family.explain: Jesus said: I do what I see my Father doing, because the Father loves me. Jesus and the Father always work together.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always work together in love.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing do we learn by watching our parents?”

illus: An illustration

A young carpenter in Ernakulam learned his trade by watching his father for years. Customers said they could not tell which chair was made by the father and which by the son. Jesus says the same about himself and the Father: whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of the Father, you give life to whom you will. Give us your life as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God (1 John 5:1). What does being born of God mean for me?
The Son does what he sees the Father doing (John 5:19). What do I see God doing in my life?
Faith conquers the world (1 John 5:4). Where do I need faith to win?
pm.resp: Lord, increase our faith.
interc: For the Church, that she may honour the Son as she honours the Father.
For those whose faith is weak or tested.
For fathers, that their children may learn from their example.
For those who feel defeated by the world.
For our group, that our faith may become victory.
pm.close: Father, your Son does your works and gives life. Make us your children by faith, and let our faith overcome the world. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses was faithful as a servant; Christ as the Son.
We are God's house if we hold firm in hope.
John points to the one standing among us, unknown.
2027-01-05.action: Light a lamp at home tonight and pray for your family.
2027-01-05.question: Is my life a house where Christ is welcome?

family.explain: John the Baptist said: someone great is among you, and I am not worthy to untie his sandal. Tomorrow we celebrate when Jesus was baptised.
family.intention: We pray that our home may be full of the light of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our home be a house of God?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Pala, an old man still plants a plantain stem in his courtyard each Denha eve and sets small lamps on it. His grandchildren, home from Bengaluru and Dubai, gather round as he calls out “El Paiya!” He says: I cannot preach, but I can light a lamp and tell them who the Light is.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stood among the crowds at the Jordan, and they did not know you. Let us know you tonight, and make our hearts your house. Amen.
share: Moses was faithful as a servant (Hebrews 3:5). Who has been a faithful servant of God in my life?
We are his house (Hebrews 3:6). How can my family become God's house?
Among you stands one whom you do not know (John 1:26). Where is Jesus standing near me, unrecognised?
pm.resp: Christ our light, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, God's house, that she may stand firm in hope.
For families keeping the Denha eve, that their lamps may be signs of faith.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism.
For those who do not yet recognise Christ among them.
For our group, that we may prepare our hearts for Denha.
pm.close: Father, tomorrow your Son is revealed at the Jordan. Make our homes your dwelling, and let us hold firm the hope we have in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul's chains helped to spread the Gospel.
He rejoiced whenever Christ was proclaimed.
John rejoiced that Jesus increased while he decreased.
2027-01-07.action: Congratulate sincerely someone whose good work is praised.
2027-01-07.question: Do I rejoice when Christ is made known through others?

family.explain: St Paul was in prison, but he was happy because more and more people were hearing about Jesus. Even in trouble, God can do good things.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are in prison for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Has something hard ever turned into something good for us?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in Thrissur was moved from the senior class she loved to teach the youngest children. She felt hurt, but she accepted. Years later three of those little ones became priests and sisters, and each named her as the first who taught them to love Jesus.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were revealed at the Jordan. Let your name be proclaimed everywhere, and free us from envy. Amen.
share: What has happened to me has helped to spread the gospel (Philippians 1:12). Can a hardship of mine become good news?
Christ is proclaimed, and in that I rejoice (Philippians 1:18). Do I rejoice in others' success in ministry?
He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). Where must I decrease?
pm.resp: Lord, let your name be proclaimed.
interc: For Christians in prison for their faith.
For preachers and catechists, that they may seek Christ's glory and not their own.
For parishes divided by rivalry.
For those whose suffering can become witness.
For our group, that Christ may increase in us.
pm.close: Father, let your Son be proclaimed in every way. Free us from rivalry and make us glad witnesses. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Nathan's courage led David to repentance.
John the Baptist died for speaking the truth.
The Church's prayer freed Peter from prison.
2027-01-08.action: Correct one wrong gently and honestly today.
2027-01-08.question: Do I stay silent when I should speak the truth with love?

family.explain: John the Baptist told King Herod that he was doing wrong. Herod put John in prison. John was brave because he loved God and the truth.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard to tell the truth? How can we be brave?”

illus: An illustration

Some years ago a young Syro-Malabar priest in a North Indian mission spoke out against a landlord who was cheating poor tribal labourers. He received threats and was transferred for his safety. Years later the labourers' children, now educated, invited him back as chief guest. They said: you were our John the Baptist.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John the Baptist prepared your way and bore witness to the truth even to death. Give us his courage and his humility. Amen.
share: Nathan said, “You are the man!” (2 Samuel 12:7). Do I accept correction when I am wrong?
“Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you” (Jeremiah 1:8). What fear keeps me from witnessing?
The church prayed fervently for Peter (Acts 12:5). For whom should our group pray fervently?
pm.resp: Lord, make us brave witnesses.
interc: For the persecuted Church, especially in Asia and Africa.
For prophets in our time who speak the truth to power.
For rulers, that they may listen to conscience.
For those who have been silenced, threatened or imprisoned.
For our group, that we may speak the truth with love.
pm.close: Lord God, John the Baptist gave his life for the truth. Strengthen us to witness to Christ without fear, and protect all who suffer for his name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Even John the Baptist had a moment of doubt.
Jesus answers with deeds: the blind see, the poor hear good news.
Heaven sings without ceasing: Holy, holy, holy.
2027-01-09.action: Do one work of mercy today so that someone sees Christ at work.
2027-01-09.question: Do I bring my doubts honestly to Jesus?

family.explain: John asked: Jesus, are you really the one God sent? Jesus said: look! The blind see, the lame walk, the sick are healed, the poor hear good news.
family.intention: We pray for people who are blind, lame or sick.
family.ask: Ask: “How can people see Jesus at work in our family?”

illus: An illustration

A young woman from Kottayam working as a nurse in Germany lost her faith during the pandemic. One night a dying patient asked her to pray with him. She did, haltingly, and saw his face fill with peace. She said later: I asked God if he was real, and he answered through a dying man.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John asked if you were the one to come, and you answered with deeds of love. Answer our doubts too, and let us sing Holy, holy, holy. Amen.
share: Are you the one who is to come? (Luke 7:19). What questions do I bring to Jesus?
Go and tell John what you have seen (Luke 7:22). What have I seen Jesus do?
Holy, holy, holy (Revelation 4:8). How does the worship of heaven change my view of my troubles?
pm.resp: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.
interc: For those struggling with doubt, that they may meet Christ in his works of mercy.
For the blind, the lame and the sick.
For the poor, that they may hear good news through the Church.
For prisoners, as John was.
For our group, that our worship may join heaven's song.
pm.close: Father, your Son showed John the signs of his kingdom. Show us his works, strengthen our faith, and let us praise you with all the hosts of heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Faith gives the eyes of the heart to see.
Christ is head over all things for the Church.
The one from above is above all.
2027-01-11.action: Give Christ the first moment of your day tomorrow.
2027-01-11.question: Is Christ really above all in my life?

family.explain: John the Baptist said: Jesus comes from heaven, and he is above everyone. The Father loves him and has put everything in his hands.
family.intention: We pray that Jesus may be first in our family.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we put Jesus first in our day?”

illus: An illustration

A businessman in Thodupuzha keeps a small rule: the first call he makes each morning is to God, five minutes of prayer before his phone rings. He says: if Christ is not first in my day, he will not be first in my decisions.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are above all, head of your Body the Church. Enlighten the eyes of our hearts as we gather. Amen.
share: With the eyes of your heart enlightened (Ephesians 1:18). What do I need to see with faith?
Head over all things for the church (Ephesians 1:22). How do I love the Church as Christ's Body?
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life (John 3:36). How strong is my belief?
pm.resp: Lord, be first in our lives.
interc: For the Church, the Body of Christ, that she may be united under her Head.
For those whose priorities have pushed God aside.
For those seeking hope.
For catechumens learning to know Christ.
For our group, that Christ may be first among us.
pm.close: Father, you raised Christ and made him head over all things. Enlighten our hearts and keep him first in our lives. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We are truly children of God.
The Son came to destroy the works of the devil.
Christ silences evil and sets people free.
2027-01-12.action: When tempted today, say: I am a child of God.
2027-01-12.question: Do I live as a child of God, or as if sin were my way of life?

family.explain: St John says: see how much God loves us! He calls us his children, and we really are!
family.intention: We pray for children who feel unloved.
family.ask: Ask: “How does it feel to be God's child?”

illus: An illustration

A teenager in Irinjalakuda told his catechism teacher that he felt worthless after failing his exams. She wrote 1 John 3:1 on a card and asked him to read it every morning. Months later he showed her the worn card: it says I am a child of God, and that is what I am. That changed how I see myself.

pm.open: Father, see what love you have given us: we are your children. Free us from all evil as we gather in Jesus' name. Amen.
share: We are called children of God, and that is what we are (1 John 3:1). Do I believe this?
The Son of God was revealed to destroy the works of the devil (1 John 3:8). Where do I need his victory?
I know who you are, the Holy One of God (Mark 1:24). Do I recognise Jesus as the Holy One?
pm.resp: Father, deliver us from evil.
interc: For children everywhere, that they may know they are loved by God.
For those oppressed by evil, addiction or fear.
For priests who minister deliverance and healing.
For those who have lost their sense of dignity.
For our group, that we may live as God's children.
pm.close: Father, you made us your children in Christ. Keep us from evil and let us live in your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At Cana Jesus revealed his glory.
Mary says: do whatever he tells you.
Cana points to the marriage supper of the Lamb.
2027-01-13.action: Do one thing Jesus asks of you that you have been delaying.
2027-01-13.question: Where has the wine run out in my life or family?

family.explain: At a wedding the wine ran out. Mary told Jesus, and told the servants: do whatever he tells you. Jesus turned water into the best wine!
family.intention: We pray for married couples and newly-weds.
family.ask: Ask: “What is Jesus telling our family to do?”

illus: An illustration

A couple in Changanassery, married twenty years, felt their love had gone flat. On their anniversary they went to Holy Qurbana together, then sat before a picture of Cana and prayed: we have no wine. They began praying together each night. A year later they said: the water of ordinary days has started to taste like wine again.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, at Cana you turned water into wine at your Mother's request. Look at what is empty in our lives, and fill it with your joy. Amen.
share: They have no wine (John 2:3). Where has the wine run out for me?
Do whatever he tells you (John 2:5). What is Jesus telling me?
Blessed are those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). How do I prepare for Holy Communion?
pm.resp: Mary, Mother of Jesus, pray for us.
interc: For married couples, that their love may be renewed.
For families facing shortage, shame or debt.
For engaged couples preparing for marriage.
For the Church, the bride of the Lamb.
For our group, that we may do whatever Jesus tells us.
pm.close: Father, at Cana your Son revealed his glory. Through Mary's prayers, fill our emptiness with his joy and prepare us for the wedding feast of heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus cleanses his Father's house.
His body is the true Temple, destroyed and raised.
Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit.
2027-01-14.action: Give up one habit that harms your body.
2027-01-14.question: Do I treat my body as a temple of the Holy Spirit?

family.explain: People were buying and selling in God's house. Jesus chased them out because he loved his Father's house. Our bodies are God's house too!
family.intention: We pray that we may take good care of our bodies and our churches.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we take care of our bodies as God's temple?”

illus: An illustration

St Devasahayam was born Neelakanta Pillai near Nagercoil. After his Baptism he took the name Lazarus, Devasahayam in Tamil and Malayalam, meaning “God is my help”. Arrested in 1749, he was paraded through towns and kept in chains for nearly three years, praying and encouraging those who came to him. He was shot dead at Aralvaimozhy in 1752, and was canonised in 2022.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, zeal for your Father's house consumed you. Cleanse our hearts and make us your temple as we gather. Amen.
share: Stop making my Father's house a marketplace (John 2:16). How do I behave in God's house?
He was speaking of the temple of his body (John 2:21). How does Jesus' body meet me?
Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19). How do I honour my body?
pm.resp: Lord, make us your temple.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a house of prayer.
For young people, that they may honour their bodies.
For those struggling with addiction.
For the Church in India, through St Devasahayam.
For our group, that we may glorify God in our bodies.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the true Temple, and you have made our bodies temples of your Spirit. Cleanse us and help us glorify you in our bodies. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus forgives Peter and entrusts him with the flock.
Paul, once a persecutor, is called by grace.
Through them the Gospel reaches every nation.
2027-01-15.action: Pray today for the Pope and our Major Archbishop.
2027-01-15.question: How would I answer if Jesus asked me: do you love me?

family.explain: Peter had said he did not know Jesus. After Easter Jesus asked him three times: do you love me? Peter said yes, and Jesus asked him to take care of his people.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and for our bishops and priests.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show Jesus that we love him?”

illus: An illustration

Under the high altar of St Peter's Basilica in Rome lie the bones of the fisherman who denied Jesus. Above them rises Michelangelo's dome. Pilgrims from Kerala who stand there often say the same thing: if Jesus could build all this on a man who failed him, he can build something on me.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you asked Peter: do you love me? Ask us too, and help us answer with our lives. Amen.
share: Simon, do you love me? (John 21:15). How do I answer Jesus?
God called me through his grace (Galatians 1:15). How has grace changed my life?
God shows no partiality (Acts 10:34). Whom do I exclude?
pm.resp: Lord, you know that we love you.
interc: For the Pope, Successor of Peter.
For our Major Archbishop and bishops.
For missionaries who carry the Gospel to the nations.
For those who have denied or persecuted the faith, that they may be transformed.
For our group, that we may love Jesus above all.
pm.close: Father, you built your Church on the faith of Peter and the preaching of Paul. Keep us in their faith, and make us love your Son above all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God reveals himself to the little ones.
Christ emptied himself, taking the form of a slave.
Come to me, and I will give you rest.
2027-01-16.action: Do one humble service today without being seen.
2027-01-16.question: What burden am I carrying alone that Jesus wants to share?

family.explain: Jesus said: come to me, all who are tired, and I will give you rest. I am gentle and humble.
family.intention: We pray for people who are tired and sad.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes you tired or worried? Let us give it to Jesus.”

illus: An illustration

Farmers in Kuttanad used to yoke a young bullock beside an old, steady one, so that the young one would learn the pace and the path. The yoke was not a punishment; it was a school. Jesus says: take my yoke and learn from me; walk beside me and you will find your pace.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, we come to you tired and burdened. Give us rest as we gather. Amen.
share: You have revealed these things to infants (Matthew 11:25). Am I little enough to receive?
He emptied himself (Philippians 2:7). Where do I need to let go of pride?
Come to me… and I will give you rest (Matthew 11:28). What burden do I bring?
pm.resp: Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, make our hearts like yours.
interc: For the weary and overburdened.
For caregivers of the sick and elderly.
For the proud and self-sufficient, that they may become little.
For those who serve in hidden ways.
For our group, that we may learn humility from Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son emptied himself and gives rest to the weary. Make us humble like him and let us find rest in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Nineveh believed God and turned from evil.
God relented; mercy is his delight.
Jesus came to call sinners.
2027-01-18.action: Keep today's fast and turn from one sin.
2027-01-18.question: What evil way must I turn from during these three days?

family.explain: Jonah told the people of Nineveh: God is angry with your sins! The king and all the people said sorry and fasted. God saw them change and forgave them.
family.intention: We pray for our city and country to turn to God.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we say sorry to God for, as a family?”

illus: An illustration

During Moonnu Nombu at Kuravilangad, pilgrims walk barefoot through the night, and on the third day men carry a large model ship around the church, remembering Jonah. An old pilgrim said: I come every year, not to see the ship, but to bring my sins and leave them with God, as Nineveh did.

pm.open: Merciful God, as we begin the fast of the Ninevites, turn our hearts to you and have mercy on us. Amen.
share: The people of Nineveh believed God (Jonah 3:5). Do I take God's word seriously?
God changed his mind about the calamity (Jonah 3:10). Do I believe in God's mercy?
I desire mercy, not sacrifice (Matthew 9:13). Is my fast making me more merciful?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that these three days may bring true conversion.
For our nation and our cities, that they may turn to God.
For sinners far from God, that they may hear Christ's call.
For the unity of Christians.
For our group, that our fasting may make us merciful.
pm.close: Lord God, you spared Nineveh when it repented. Spare us and renew us through prayer and fasting. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God hears from heaven and forgives those who turn.
Confess your sins and pray for one another.
Jesus is the Lamb who takes away the world's sin.
2027-01-19.action: Make your confession during these three days.
2027-01-19.question: What sin have I not yet brought honestly to God?

family.explain: John the Baptist pointed to Jesus and said: there is the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world!
family.intention: We pray for all who will go to confession during these three days.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we say sorry to each other at home today?”

illus: An illustration

A man who had not confessed for twenty years came to the confessional on the second day of Moonnu Nombu at a parish in Kottayam. Afterwards he sat in the church and wept. He told the priest: I fasted for two days to prepare, but the real food I received was forgiveness.

pm.open: Lamb of God, who take away the sin of the world, have mercy on us as we confess our sins together. Amen.
share: Hear from heaven and forgive (2 Chronicles 6:27). Do I trust God to forgive?
Confess your sins to one another (James 5:16). When did I last make a good confession?
Here is the Lamb of God (John 1:29). What sin do I need to give to the Lamb?
pm.resp: Lamb of God, have mercy on us.
interc: For all who will make their confession during the fast.
For priests who hear confessions.
For the sick, that they may receive the Anointing and be healed.
For those who have wandered from the faith.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world. Give us humble hearts to confess and joyful hearts to receive your mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God says: I will love them freely.
The forgiven woman showed great love.
Love covers a multitude of sins.
2027-01-20.action: Do one generous act of love for someone in your family today.
2027-01-20.question: Does my love show how much I have been forgiven?

family.explain: A woman cried at Jesus' feet because she was sorry. Jesus forgave her, and she loved him very much.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops named Sebastian and for soldiers and police.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show love to each other at the end of the fast?”

illus: An illustration

At the end of Moonnu Nombu a family in Ernakulam has a custom: they do not break the fast with a feast first, but with a visit to a lonely elderly neighbour, bringing food. The mother says: we fasted to grow in love; so the first meal belongs to someone who has no one.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you forgave much and received great love. As our fast ends, fill us with your love. Amen.
share: I will love them freely (Hosea 14:4). Do I let God love me freely?
She has shown great love (Luke 7:47). How does my love show God's forgiveness?
Love covers a multitude of sins (1 Peter 4:8). Whose faults can my love cover?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to love.
interc: For the fruits of the Three Days' Fast in our Church.
For Mar Sebastian Vadakkel, Mar Sebastian Adayanthrath, Mar Sebastian Vaniyapurackal and Mar Sebastian Pozholiparampil.
For soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
For those judged harshly by others.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, you love us freely and forgive much. Let the love we have received overflow to others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked.
He casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
Heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.
2027-01-21.action: Contact one person who has drifted from the Church.
2027-01-21.question: Do I share God's joy when a sinner returns, or do I grumble?

family.explain: A shepherd lost one sheep. He looked everywhere until he found it, then carried it home happily. God is that happy when someone comes back to him!
family.intention: We pray for people who are lost and far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “How did the fast help our family?”

illus: An illustration

In Kerala fishing villages, when a boat lost at sea for days finally returns, the whole beach runs to meet it, church bells ring and there is a feast. A fisherman said: that is how heaven is when one of us comes back to God.

pm.open: God of mercy, the fast is over and your mercy remains. Fill us with your joy over every sinner who returns. Amen.
share: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked (Ezekiel 33:11). Do I believe God wants me to live?
You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea (Micah 7:19). What sin do I need to leave there?
Rejoice with me (Luke 15:6). Do I rejoice when others return to God?
pm.resp: Lord, we rejoice in your mercy.
interc: In thanksgiving for the graces of the Three Days' Fast.
For those still far from God.
For priests who seek the lost.
For families waiting for a member to return.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, you delight in showing mercy. Keep us in the joy of your forgiveness and make us seekers of the lost. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The four Gospels flow like rivers from Christ.
Four living creatures stand for the four Evangelists.
Good soil holds the word fast and bears fruit.
2027-01-22.action: Begin reading one Gospel, a chapter a day.
2027-01-22.question: What kind of soil is my heart for God's word?

family.explain: A farmer threw seeds. Some fell on the path, some on rocks, some in thorns, and some in good soil, where they grew big. Our hearts can be good soil for God's word!
family.intention: We pray that all people may hear the Gospel.
family.ask: Ask: “Do you know the names of the four Gospel writers?”

illus: An illustration

In many old churches in Kerala the four Evangelists are painted around the dome: a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle. A grandfather in Ankamaly used to point them out to his grandchildren and say: four writers, one Jesus. Read all four, and you will know him better.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your word is a seed. Make our hearts good soil as we gather to hear it. Amen.
share: A river divides into four branches (Genesis 2:10). How has the Gospel reached me?
Four living creatures around the throne (Revelation 4:6–7). Which Evangelist speaks most to me?
Hold it fast in an honest and good heart (Luke 8:15). What chokes the word in me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us good soil.
interc: For preachers and teachers of the Gospel.
For Bible translators and those who spread Scripture.
For those who have never heard the Gospel.
For Christian unity around the word of God.
For our group, that we may bear fruit with patience.
pm.close: Father, through the Evangelists you gave us the Gospel of your Son. Make our hearts fruitful soil for your word. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Salvation is near, on our lips and in our hearts.
Confess Jesus as Lord and believe he is risen.
Everyone who calls on the Lord shall be saved.
2027-01-23.action: Say aloud in prayer today: Jesus, you are Lord.
2027-01-23.question: Do I confess with my lips what I believe in my heart?

family.explain: St Paul says: if you say with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him, you will be saved. Anyone who calls on Jesus will be saved!
family.intention: We pray for people who feel far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “Let us all say together: Jesus is Lord!”

illus: An illustration

A woman dying of cancer in a Thrissur hospital could no longer speak sentences. Each time the chaplain visited, she whispered one word: Eesho. He said: her whole theology was in that one word, and it was enough. Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your word is near us. We confess that you are Lord, and we call on your name. Amen.
share: The word is near you (Romans 10:8). Do I think God is far away?
Confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord (Romans 10:9). Where do I keep silent about my faith?
If you choose, you can make me clean (Mark 1:40). What do I need to ask Jesus today?
pm.resp: Jesus, you are Lord.
interc: For all who do not yet confess Jesus as Lord.
For people excluded by illness or stigma.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism.
For Christian unity in confessing one Lord.
For our group, that we may call on Jesus in every need.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and made him Lord. Let every tongue confess him, and let all who call on him be saved. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God called Moses and Saul by name.
Paul: by the grace of God I am what I am.
The latecomers in the vineyard receive the same generous wage.
2027-01-25.action: Rejoice sincerely in someone else's blessing today.
2027-01-25.question: Do I resent God's generosity to others?
kidsaint: He was angry with Christians until Jesus spoke to him on the road. Then he became Jesus' best messenger. Lesson: God can use anyone, even someone who started badly!
2027-01-25.special: Conversion of St Paul. Conclusion of the Church Unity Octave.
term: God's gift of his own life and help, given without our earning it.

family.explain: A farm owner paid everyone the same, even those who came to work late. Some were cross. God is generous to everyone!
family.intention: We pray for Christians of all Churches, that they may be one.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be happy when good things happen to others?”

illus: An illustration

A man from Changanassery was baptized at sixty-eight after years of mocking his wife's faith. At his first Communion he wept and said: I came at the eleventh hour, and the Lord gave me the full wage. His wife said: I prayed forty years; it was worth every day.

pm.open: Lord, you call us by name and give us grace we do not earn. Make us grateful and generous. Amen.
share: Moses, Moses! (Exodus 3:4). Do I hear God calling me by name?
Who are you, Lord? (Acts 9:5). Do I know Jesus personally?
Are you envious because I am generous? (Matthew 20:15). Where am I envious?
pm.resp: Lord, by your grace we are what we are.
interc: For the unity of Christians, at the end of the Unity Octave.
For those who persecute the Church.
For late converts and those returning to faith.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism.
For our group, that we may rejoice in one another's gifts.
pm.close: Father, your grace is generous to all. Free us from envy and make us witnesses of your mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Faith that works, love that labours, hope that endures.
The word came in power and the Holy Spirit.
Whoever is from God hears the words of God.
2027-01-26.action: Do one concrete service for your neighbourhood today.
2027-01-26.question: Does my faith show in work, my love in labour, my hope in endurance?

family.explain: St Paul thanked God for Christians who worked hard because of their faith, helped others because of their love, and never gave up because of their hope.
family.intention: We pray for India on Republic Day.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family help our village or town this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a panchayat near Thodupuzha, a group of parishioners spent Republic Day cleaning the public well and the path to the government school, working side by side with neighbours of other faiths. One of them said: we heard Paul's words about the labour of love at Qurbana, and thought this was a good place to begin.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, let your word come to us in power and in the Holy Spirit, and bless our nation. Amen.
share: Your work of faith and labor of love (1 Thessalonians 1:3). Where does my faith become work?
You received the word with joy (1 Thessalonians 1:6). Do I receive God's word gladly?
Whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47). Do I listen to God in my decisions?
pm.resp: Lord, make us faithful.
interc: For India on Republic Day: for justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
For the President, the Prime Minister and all who govern.
For religious freedom and harmony among communities.
For bishops, through Sts Timothy and Titus.
For our group, that our faith may be active in love.
pm.close: Father, your word gives life to your people. Make us faithful disciples and good citizens. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The time is short; hold the world lightly.
Undivided devotion to the Lord.
There is need of only one thing.
2027-01-27.action: Give ten minutes today to silent listening to the Gospel.
2027-01-27.question: What worries distract me from the one thing necessary?

family.explain: Martha was very busy cooking for Jesus, and Mary sat and listened to him. Jesus said listening to him is the most important thing.
family.intention: We pray for religious sisters and brothers.
family.ask: Ask: “When can our family sit quietly with Jesus every day?”

illus: An illustration

A mother of four in Pala, always rushing, decided to keep the first ten minutes after the family rosary for silent reading of the Gospel before starting the evening work. She said: the dishes still get done, but now I do them with a quiet heart.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we sit at your feet. Speak to us and calm our anxious hearts. Amen.
share: The present form of this world is passing away (1 Corinthians 7:31). What do I cling to?
Unhindered devotion to the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:35). What divides my heart?
Mary has chosen the better part (Luke 10:42). How can I choose it today?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the one thing necessary.
interc: For consecrated men and women.
For married couples, that they may grow in devotion to God together.
For those overwhelmed by work and worry.
For vocations to religious life.
For our group, that we may listen before we act.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the better part that will not be taken from us. Keep our hearts undivided in his love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's promise to Abraham is fulfilled in Christ.
Martha brought her grief and her faith to Jesus.
Jesus is the resurrection and the life.
2027-01-28.question: Do I believe Jesus is the resurrection, even in my sorrows?

family.explain: Martha's brother had died and she was very sad. Jesus told her: I am the resurrection and the life. Martha said: Yes, Lord, I believe!
family.intention: We pray for families who are grieving, and for students through St Thomas Aquinas.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we remember who is with God? Let us pray for them.”

illus: An illustration

At a funeral in Changanassery, the widow asked the priest to read not a sad passage but John 11. When the words “I am the resurrection and the life” were read, she said quietly with Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe. Her children said later that they learned their faith in that moment.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, we bring you our sorrows and our faith. Amen.
share: To your offspring, that is, to one person, who is Christ (Galatians 3:16). Do I see Christ as the centre of God's plan?
Lord, if you had been here (John 11:21). What sorrow do I bring to Jesus?
Do you believe this? (John 11:26). How do I answer Jesus today?
pm.resp: Lord, we believe.
interc: For the grieving and the dying.
For those who have lost hope.
For theologians and students, through St Thomas Aquinas.
For the departed of our families.
For our group, that we may confess Christ like Martha.
pm.close: Father, in your Son every promise is fulfilled. Raise us with him to eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abel's and Naboth's innocent blood cried out.
Stephen saw heaven opened and forgave his killers.
Jesus' blood speaks a better word: forgiveness.
2027-01-29.action: Pray by name for someone who has wronged you.
2027-01-29.question: Whom do I need to forgive as Stephen forgave?

family.explain: People threw stones at Stephen because he loved Jesus. As he was dying, he prayed: Lord, forgive them. He was like Jesus!
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith today.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we forgive someone who hurt us, like Stephen did?”

illus: An illustration

In 1999 the Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two young sons were burned to death in Odisha. His widow Gladys publicly forgave the killers and stayed on to serve leprosy patients. Many in India who had never read the Gospel learned from her what Christian forgiveness means. Stephen's prayer is still being prayed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, give us the faith and forgiveness of St Stephen. Amen.
share: Your brother's blood is crying out (Genesis 4:10). Do I hear the cry of the innocent?
His face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). Does Christ shine in me under pressure?
Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60). Whom must I forgive?
pm.resp: Lord, receive our spirit.
interc: For persecuted Christians throughout the world.
For those falsely accused and unjustly condemned.
For those who persecute, that they may be converted like Saul.
For deacons, following St Stephen.
For our group, that we may forgive.
pm.close: Father, your Son's blood speaks forgiveness. Through St Stephen, make us witnesses of that word. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We are members of one another; speak truth and build up.
Do not let the sun go down on your anger.
Forgive, as the Father forgives you.
2027-01-30.action: Make peace with someone before the day ends.
2027-01-30.question: Is there anger I have carried past many sunsets?

family.explain: St Paul says: do not stay angry; be kind and forgive each other, because God forgave us.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always make peace before bedtime.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family we need to forgive before we sleep tonight?”

illus: An illustration

An old couple in Thrissur, married for sixty years, were asked their secret. The wife said: on our wedding night we promised never to sleep without saying sorry. Some nights we stayed up very late, she laughed, but the sun never set on our anger.

pm.open: Our Father, teach us to pray in secret and to forgive from the heart. Amen.
share: Do not let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:26). What anger am I carrying?
Your Father knows what you need (Matthew 6:8). Do I trust the Father?
If you forgive others (Matthew 6:14). Whom must I forgive before I pray the Our Father again?
pm.resp: Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For families divided by anger.
For those who cannot forgive.
For peace in our homes and parishes.
For those whose words wound others.
For our group, that we may build one another up.
pm.close: Father, you have forgiven us in Christ. Make us kind, tenderhearted and forgiving. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to you all. On this first day of the year the Church does not begin with our plans but with a Name: the Holy Name of Jesus. Eight days after his birth, the Child was circumcised and named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21).

In the Bible a name is never only a label. In the first reading God changes Abram's name to Abraham, father of a multitude, and gives him the covenant (Genesis 17:5). And through Isaiah he says to his people: I have called you by name, you are mine (Isaiah 43:1). Each of us was called by name at Baptism. God knows you, not as a number, but by name.

The name Jesus means the Lord saves. The angel says to Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). We may want many things from the new year: health, a job, success for our children. Jesus comes first to save us from sin, the root of every other sorrow.

St Paul tells us how this Name was won. Christ Jesus emptied himself, took the form of a slave, humbled himself and became obedient to death on a cross. Therefore God highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name (Philippians 2:7–9). The way to glory is the way of humility.

Today is also the last Friday of Nativity, when our Church honours the Divine Motherhood of Mary. She who gave Jesus his human flesh is truly the Mother of God, and she stands with the Apostles in prayer (Acts 1:14). Let us begin this year with her.

So let us make a simple resolution: to call on the Name of Jesus every day. Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Let this Name be on our lips in joy and in trouble, and this year will be blessed. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Jesus' name day! The name Jesus means God saves us. Let us say his name with love every day.
Do you know your own name's meaning? Ask your parents tonight, and thank God for calling you by name.

intro: On the eighth day the Child received the name Jesus, which means “the Lord saves”. We begin the year by calling on that name.

sub: The angel chose it before his birth (Matthew 1:21).
His name tells us his mission.
points.apply: Learn the meaning of your own baptismal name.

sub: He humbled himself to the cross.
points.apply: Bow your head whenever the name of Jesus is spoken at the Holy Qurbana.

sub: A year lived in his name.
points.apply: Begin each day this year with the name of Jesus.

concl: The name of Jesus is our programme for the new year: God saves.
Whatever this year holds, we face it in his name.
opts.resolve: This year I will begin and end each day by calling on the name of Jesus.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to all of you. On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21). The name means the Lord saves. God chose it himself.

In the Bible a name is a mission. The angel told Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). Every time we say the name of Jesus, we confess what he came to do.

Paul tells us that because Jesus humbled himself to the cross, God gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend (Philippians 2:9–10). That is why we bow our heads at his name.

Peter, standing before the council, said: there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). We do not know what this year will bring. But we know the name in which we will face it.

So let us begin the year as the Church begins it: in the name of Jesus. Let it be the first word on our lips in the morning and the last at night. And may the Lord bless us and keep us in his name throughout this year. Amen.

opts.a: Mary, Mother of God, and the year ahead
intro: In 431 the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God. The first day of the year belongs to her and to her Son.

sub: Not mother of a man only.
The Son she bore is God.
Ephesus defended Christ by honouring Mary.
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, weighing the words “Mother of God”.

sub: Mary keeps it in her heart.
A heart that remembers God's deeds.
points.apply: Each night this year, recall one thing God did that day.

sub: So that we might be children.
points.apply: Put your family under Mary's protection for the year.

concl: Mary, Mother of God, is also our mother.
With her we begin the year pondering God's works in our hearts.
opts.resolve: I will entrust this year to Mary, Mother of God, and keep a habit of thanksgiving each night.
homily: Dear friends, today the Church greets Mary with her greatest title: Mother of God. In the year 431 the bishops gathered at Ephesus defended this title, because the Child she bore is not a man who later became God, but the eternal Son of God made man. Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
Paul says: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). God did not come among us from nowhere. He came through a mother, through a family, through a people.

When the shepherds told what they had seen, Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). She did not understand everything, but she kept it and turned it over in prayer. That is a good way to live a year.
Paul adds: because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father (Galatians 4:6). Through Mary's Son we become children of God.

So let us begin the year with her. Let us ask Mary, Mother of God, to keep our families, and let us learn from her to ponder each day what God has done. And may the Lord bless us and keep us, and give us peace. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, on this Second Sunday of Nativity all our readings take place in the presence of God. Moses comes down from Mount Sinai after forty days, and the skin of his face shines because he has been talking with God (Exodus 34:29). He does not even know it.

The boy Samuel sleeps in the temple where the ark of God is. Three times the Lord calls him, and three times he runs to old Eli. Finally he learns to say: speak, for your servant is listening (1 Samuel 3:10). Those who stay near God are changed by him, and they learn to listen.

In the Gospel Jesus is twelve. After the Passover he stays behind in Jerusalem. For three days Mary and Joseph search for him with great anxiety. Every parent here knows that feeling. They find him in the Temple, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions.

His first words in the Gospel are: why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house? (Luke 2:49). At twelve, Jesus knows who his Father is. And yet he goes down with them to Nazareth and is obedient to them, and grows in wisdom and in years and in favour with God and people (Luke 2:51–52). Holiness does not despise ordinary family life; it is lived there.

St Paul tells us how to live this: present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship. Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds (Romans 12:1–2). Our whole life becomes worship.

Today we also remember St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, a son of our Church who stayed close to God in prayer and built schools beside churches so that children could grow in wisdom. Let us ask for his spirit: to listen to God, to love the Father's house, and to serve our families with obedience and love. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was twelve, Mary and Joseph lost him for three days! They found him in the Temple, learning about God. Then he went home and obeyed them.
Let us love to come to church, the Father's house, and let us obey our parents with a smile.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed feast of Denha to you. Denha means dawn, rising, manifestation. Our Church celebrates today the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God was revealed.

Look at the scene in Mark. Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptised by John. Just as he is coming up out of the water, he sees the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice comes from heaven: you are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased (Mark 1:10–11). Son, Spirit and Father: the Holy Trinity is revealed.

The first reading takes us to Sinai. The LORD descended upon it in fire; the mountain shook violently, and the people had to keep away (Exodus 19:18). At the Jordan God comes down again, but now so gently: a dove, a voice of love, a man standing in the river among sinners. What was terrifying at Sinai becomes tender at the Jordan.

Why was Jesus baptised? He had no sin. He went down into the water to stand with us sinners and to sanctify the waters for our Baptism. The prophet Joel had promised: I will pour out my spirit on all flesh (Joel 2:28). That outpouring begins with Jesus and reaches us in Baptism and Confirmation.

Our ancestors kept this feast beautifully. They lit lamps on plantain stems and walked around crying El Paiya, God is light. On the eve they bathed in rivers and ponds, remembering the Jordan. These customs said: we are baptised; we are children of light.

St Paul tells Timothy: rekindle the gift of God that is within you (2 Timothy 1:6). Many of us were baptised as infants and rarely think of it. Today, let us remember: God has said to you, you are my beloved son, my beloved daughter. Let us live as people who have heard that voice. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Denha! Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. The Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and God said: you are my beloved Son!
When you were baptised, God said the same to you: you are my beloved child. Ask your parents when your Baptism day is!

intro: Isaiah prayed: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down.” At the Jordan the prayer is answered.

points.apply: Thank God for coming close to you.
Make the sign of the cross slowly and with faith today.

sub: He sanctifies the water for us.
points.apply: Bless yourself with holy water when you enter church.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opens and the Trinity is revealed.
In Baptism heaven opened for us too.
opts.resolve: I will make the sign of the cross with faith, remembering that heaven opened at my Baptism.
homily: Dear friends, long ago Isaiah cried out: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down (Isaiah 64:1). Israel longed for God to come close. At the Jordan the prayer is answered: as Jesus came up from the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him (Mark 1:10).

This is the great manifestation of the Trinity. The Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends, and the Father's voice says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:17). Every time we make the sign of the cross, we confess what was revealed at the Jordan.
Jesus did not need to be cleansed. The Fathers said: he went into the water not to be made holy by it, but to make the waters holy for us. From that day, water became the doorway into God's life.

Paul says: he saved us through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). What happened at the Jordan happened to us at the font. Heaven opened over us; the Father called us his children.
Today let us thank God for our Baptism, make the sign of the cross with faith, and come to the Holy Qurbana as children of an open heaven. Amen.

intro: Most of us were baptised as infants and remember nothing. Today the Church asks us to remember what God did.

points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it.
Live one day this week as if wearing your baptismal garment.

sub: The candle lit from the Easter flame.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises tonight: I reject sin; I believe.

concl: Baptism is not only a past event but a present identity.
We live as children of God, clothed with Christ, walking in the light.
opts.resolve: This week I will find my Baptism date, thank my godparents, and renew my baptismal promises.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, most of us were baptised as infants. We do not remember the water, the oil or the candle. Today, as we celebrate the Lord's own baptism, the Church invites us to remember what God did to us.

Paul asks: do you not know that all of us who have been baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death? We were buried with him by baptism, so that we too might walk in newness of life (Romans 6:3–4). The font is both a tomb and a womb.

He also says: as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:27). That is why we received a white garment. We are called to wear Christ every day, at home, at work, in our words.

At Baptism a candle was lit for us, and our godparents spoke promises on our behalf: to reject sin and to believe. Now that we are grown, those promises are ours to keep. Once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light (Ephesians 5:8).
So let us find the date of our Baptism, thank our godparents, and tonight renew our promises: I reject sin; I believe in God. Then come to the Holy Qurbana as children of the light. Amen.
Dear brothers and sisters, in the season of Denha the Church keeps asking: who is this Jesus revealed at the Jordan? Today the readings answer with the name of God.

At the burning bush Moses asks God's name. God replies: I AM WHO I AM… Thus you shall say to the Israelites, I AM has sent me to you (Exodus 3:14). God is not one being among many; he is the One who simply is. Everything else comes and goes; he remains.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks in the same way. You are from below, I am from above. You will die in your sins unless you believe that I am he (John 8:23–24). In the Greek, Jesus simply says: I am. His hearers understood that he was speaking the name of God.

Then he says something deeper still: when you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he (John 8:28). We would expect God to show himself in power. Instead he shows himself on the Cross. There the I AM of the burning bush is revealed as Love that gives itself.

The Book of Revelation praises him: I am the Alpha and the Omega, who is and who was and who is to come (Revelation 1:8). And it calls him the one who loves us and freed us from our sins by his blood (Revelation 1:5).

Our world changes quickly: jobs, technology, relationships. Where do we stand? On the One who is. Let us make an act of faith each day this week: Jesus, I believe that you are the Lord, and let us look at the Cross where his name shines most brightly. Amen.
kids: Children, God told Moses his name: I AM. That means God is always there! Jesus said the same: I am. Jesus is God with us.
When you feel alone, say: Jesus, you are here. He always is!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today's readings are about God's choice. Moses, near death, calls Joshua before all Israel: be strong and bold… it is the LORD who goes before you; he will not fail you or forsake you (Deuteronomy 31:7–8). Joshua's name means the LORD saves, the same name as Jesus.

Through Isaiah God speaks to his discouraged people in exile: you are my servant, I have chosen you and not cast you off; do not fear, for I am with you (Isaiah 41:9–10). Many of us feel we are not good enough. God does not choose us because we are perfect, but because he loves us and has a mission for us.

In the Gospel Jesus goes up the mountain and calls to him those whom he wanted. He appoints the Twelve to be with him and to be sent out (Mark 3:13–14). Fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot: ordinary people, chosen.

Paul tells us what being chosen did to him. Everything he once boasted of, his birth, his zeal, his religious achievements, he now counts as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord (Philippians 3:8). And he has not stopped: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal (Philippians 3:13–14).

Tomorrow we begin the Three Days' Fast, the fast of the Ninevites. Our ancestors kept it with great devotion; many go on pilgrimage to Kuravilangad and other churches. It is our answer to God's choice: conversion, prayer and fasting.
So let us not sit back. Let us count some things as loss for Christ during these three days, and press on toward the prize of God's call. Do not fear: he goes before you. Amen.
kids: Children, God told Joshua: be strong and brave, I am with you! God says the same to you.
Tomorrow the Three Days' Fast begins. What small thing can you give up for Jesus?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in Denha Christ is revealed, and today he is revealed beside a well. In Genesis Jacob, far from home, meets Rachel at a well and weeps for joy. In the Bible wells are places of meeting and of new beginnings.
The second reading explains the Samaritans: foreigners settled in Samaria who mixed the worship of the LORD with other gods. By Jesus' time Jews and Samaritans would not even share a cup.

Yet Jesus, tired, sits by Jacob's well at noon and says to a Samaritan woman: give me a drink (John 4:7). He crosses the barriers of race, religion, gender and reputation. Then he offers her living water: those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty (John 4:14).

He reads her life truthfully but without contempt. He teaches that God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth (John 4:24). And when she speaks of the Messiah, he says: I am he, the one who is speaking to you (John 4:26).

Hebrews tells us not to become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises (Hebrews 6:12). The woman did not stay still. She left her water jar and ran to the town.
We have received living water in Baptism and receive Christ in the Qurbana. Let us leave our jars, cross barriers, and bring others to the well. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked a woman for water and then gave her living water: God's love that never runs out!
Who can you be kind to this week, especially someone who is left out?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today's readings speak of forgiveness from beginning to end. In Leviticus, when the people sin, a bull is offered and the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven (Leviticus 4:20). Sin is serious; forgiveness is costly.
In exile Daniel fasts and confesses for all the people: we have sinned and done wrong. To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness (Daniel 9:5, 9). Forgiveness is never owed; it is God's mercy.

In Capernaum four friends dig through a roof to lower a paralysed man before Jesus. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic: Son, your sins are forgiven (Mark 2:5). The scribes ask: who can forgive sins but God alone? They are right; and God is standing in front of them.
Jesus says: so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, stand up, take your mat and go home (Mark 2:10–11). And the man walks out before them all.

Paul says: in the beloved Son we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins; he is the image of the invisible God (Colossians 1:14–15). Christ gave this authority to his Church. Every confession is Capernaum again.
Let us go to confession, and like the four friends, let us carry to Christ those who cannot come alone, as St John Bosco carried so many young people. Amen.
kids: Children, four friends carried a sick man to Jesus, even through the roof! Jesus forgave him and he could walk again.
Who can you help bring closer to Jesus this week?
