homily: Dear friends, at the end of the Presentation story Luke tells us about Anna. She was a prophet, widowed after only seven years of marriage, and now eighty-four years old. She never left the Temple but worshipped there with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2:36–37).

Imagine those decades of prayer. No visions, no headlines, just faithfulness. And then one day, at that very moment, she comes and sees the Child. She begins to praise God and to speak about him to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luke 2:38).
Anna teaches us that no prayer is wasted. Many grandmothers and grandfathers in our parishes are Annas: their hidden prayer carries families, vocations and the whole Church.

St Paul thanks God that the Corinthians are not lacking in any spiritual gift as they wait for the Lord (1 Corinthians 1:7). God is faithful. In Nazareth the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom (Luke 2:40). Let us ask for Anna's faithfulness and the Child's wisdom in this new year. Amen.
kids: Children, Anna was a very old lady who prayed every day. When she saw baby Jesus, she told everyone! Let us thank our grandparents who pray for us.

homily: Dear friends, in these final days of the Nativity season the Church asks: who is this Child? Jesus answers in the Gospel: the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise (John 5:19).

This is the language of perfect unity. Jesus gives life as the Father gives life. He is entrusted with judgement. And all must honour the Son just as they honour the Father (John 5:23). The Child in the manger is worthy of the same worship as the Father.
St John tells us what this means for us. Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God (1 John 5:1). Faith is not only an opinion; it is a new birth.

And this new birth is powerful: whatever is born of God conquers the world. This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith (1 John 5:4). Fears, temptations and the pressures of the world do not have the last word over a child of God.
As Denha approaches, let us renew our faith in Jesus, the Son of the Father, and live this week as children who have already won. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus always does what his Father does, because they love each other. Watch the good things your parents do, and do the same!

homily: Dear friends, tonight is the eve of Denha. The letter to the Hebrews compares Moses and Jesus. Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant. Christ was faithful over God's house as a son (Hebrews 3:5–6). The servant is honoured; the Son is the heir and builder.

Then Hebrews says something wonderful: we are his house, if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope (Hebrews 3:6). We are not only visitors in God's house. We are the house, the living temple where God dwells.

In the Gospel John the Baptist is questioned. Who are you? He refuses every title. He is only a voice. And he says: among you stands one whom you do not know (John 1:26). Jesus is already there in the crowd, unknown.

Tomorrow that hidden one will step into the Jordan, and the heavens will open. Our ancestors kept this night with lamps on plantain stems, crying El Paiya, God is light, and with a bath that recalled the Jordan. Let us light a lamp in our hearts tonight, and prepare to see him. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight is the eve of Denha! In many homes people light lamps and say: God is light! Light a lamp with your family and say thank you to Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, on the day after Denha we hear from Paul in prison. You would expect complaints. Instead he writes: what has happened to me has actually helped to spread the gospel (Philippians 1:12). The whole imperial guard knows why he is in chains, and other believers have become bolder.

Some, he says, preach Christ out of envy, trying to make his imprisonment harder. Paul's answer is astonishing: what does it matter? Christ is proclaimed in every way, and in that I rejoice (Philippians 1:18). He cares more about Christ being known than about his own reputation.

John the Baptist has the same heart. When his disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus, he says: he must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). He is the friend of the bridegroom, and his joy is complete.

In the season of Denha Christ is manifested to the world. Let us check our hearts. Envy and rivalry can enter even church work. May we rejoice whenever Christ is proclaimed, by whoever proclaims him. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul was in prison, but he was happy because people were hearing about Jesus. Let us be happy when others do good things too!

homily: Dear friends, on the Fridays of Denha the Church remembers the witnesses of Christ. Today we honour John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open at the Jordan. The readings show us what a prophet looks like.

Nathan goes to King David after his sin with Bathsheba and the murder of Uriah. He tells a story of a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb. David is furious. Then Nathan says: you are the man! (2 Samuel 12:7). Courage and wisdom bring the king to repentance.

Jeremiah is young and afraid, but God says: do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you (Jeremiah 1:8). John the Baptist was consecrated even before birth, leaping in his mother's womb before Jesus.
John told Herod: it is not lawful for you to have her (Matthew 14:4). Herod imprisoned him and, at a drunken party, to keep a foolish promise, had him beheaded. Truth spoken with love can be costly.

In Acts, James is killed and Peter imprisoned. But the church prayed fervently to God for him (Acts 12:5), and an angel set him free. Some witnesses are freed, some die, but all are held by God. Let us pray for courage to speak the truth with love, and let us pray fervently for the persecuted Church. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was very brave. He told the king the truth even when it was dangerous. Let us always tell the truth, kindly and bravely.

homily: Dear friends, from Herod's prison John the Baptist sends two disciples to Jesus with a question: are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another? (Luke 7:19). Even the great prophet who saw the heavens open has a moment of darkness.

Jesus does not scold him and does not argue. He tells the messengers: go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them (Luke 7:22). These are the signs Isaiah promised.
Then he adds: blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me (Luke 7:23). The Messiah does not always act as we expect. He comes in mercy before he comes in judgement.

The epistle opens a door in heaven. Around the throne the living creatures sing day and night: holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come (Revelation 4:8). We join that song at every Qurbana. When doubts come, let us bring them honestly to Jesus, look at his works of mercy, and lift our eyes to his throne. Amen.
kids: Children, even John the Baptist had a question for Jesus. Jesus answered: look at what I do! I help the blind and the sick. You can ask Jesus your questions too.

homily: Dear friends, Paul prays that the Ephesians may have the eyes of their heart enlightened, to know the hope to which God has called them (Ephesians 1:18). Faith is a way of seeing.

What does faith see? The power of God that raised Christ from the dead and seated him at his right hand, far above every power. And God has made him the head over all things for the church, which is his body (Ephesians 1:22–23). The Church is the Body of the risen Lord.

In the Gospel John the Baptist says: the one who comes from above is above all. The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life (John 3:31, 35–36).

In Denha we contemplate Christ revealed. The question is practical: is he really above all in my life? Above my plans, my money, my phone, my fears? Let us give him the first moment of each day this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is above everyone and everything. Let us say good morning to Jesus first thing every day!

homily: Dear friends, St John cannot contain his wonder: see what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are (1 John 3:1). Not just a name, but a reality given in Baptism.
John tells us why the Son came: the Son of God was revealed for this purpose, to destroy the works of the devil (1 John 3:8). Denha is God's revelation for our freedom.

In the synagogue a man with an unclean spirit shouts: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus says: be silent, and come out of him! And the man is freed (Mark 1:24–25). Evil recognises its Master.
We are children of God. When temptation comes, let us remember who we are. When evil oppresses, let us call on the Holy One of God. Amen.
kids: Children, God loves you so much that he calls you his child. You really are God's child! Say it today: I am God's child!

homily: Dear friends, the early Church celebrated three epiphanies: the Magi, the Jordan, and Cana. Today, in Denha, we go to the wedding at Cana. The wine runs out. For a village family that is a public shame.

Mary notices first. She says to Jesus: they have no wine (John 2:3). Then she tells the servants: do whatever he tells you (John 2:5). These are her last words in John's Gospel, and the best advice anyone has ever given.
Six stone jars are filled with water. The water becomes the best wine. Jesus did this, the first of his signs, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him (John 2:11).
Revelation shows where it leads: blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). Every Holy Qurbana is a foretaste of that feast.
When the wine of joy or love or strength runs out in our homes, let us tell Jesus through Mary, and then do whatever he tells us. Amen.
kids: Children, at a wedding there was no more wine. Mary told Jesus, and Jesus turned water into wine! Mary helps us too. Let us ask her today.

homily: Dear friends, after Cana Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for the Passover. In the Temple he finds people selling cattle, sheep and doves, and money changers at their tables. He makes a whip of cords, drives them out and says: stop making my Father's house a marketplace! (John 2:16).
The disciples remember the psalm: zeal for your house will consume me (John 2:17). Jesus burns with love for his Father's house.

When they ask for a sign, he says: destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. John explains: he was speaking of the temple of his body (John 2:19, 21). God now meets us in Jesus, crucified and risen.

St Paul applies this to us: your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit; you are not your own; you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body (1 Corinthians 6:19–20). Purity, sobriety and care for health are reverence for a temple.
Today we honour St Devasahayam, who after Baptism gave his body in martyrdom for Christ. Let us honour God's house, and the temple of our bodies. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus loved his Father's house very much. Your body is God's house too! Take good care of it, and be quiet and prayerful in church.

homily: Dear friends, on the Fridays of Denha the Church honours the great witnesses of Christ. Today: Peter and Paul, the pillars of the Church.

Peter denied Jesus three times beside a charcoal fire. After the Resurrection, beside another charcoal fire at the lake, Jesus asks him three times: Simon son of John, do you love me? Peter answers: yes, Lord; you know that I love you. And Jesus says: feed my lambs (John 21:15). Jesus builds his Church not on a perfect man but on a forgiven man who loves.

Paul tells us he once violently persecuted the Church. But God, who had set him apart before he was born and called him through his grace, revealed his Son to him (Galatians 1:15–16). Grace turned the persecutor into the apostle of the nations.

In Acts Peter preaches to a Roman family: God shows no partiality; everyone who believes receives forgiveness of sins through his name (Acts 10:34, 43). Israel's calling to be a priestly kingdom and a holy nation (Exodus 19:6) reaches all peoples.
Both died as martyrs in Rome. Let us pray today for the Pope, Peter's successor, and for our Major Archbishop. And let us answer Jesus' question from our hearts: Lord, you know that I love you. Amen.
kids: Children, Peter once said he did not know Jesus. But Jesus forgave him and asked: do you love me? Peter said yes! Jesus forgives us too. Tell Jesus today: I love you!

homily: Dear friends, Jesus prays: I thank you, Father, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants (Matthew 11:25). The revelation of Denha is received by the humble, not by the proud.

Then he invites us: come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:28–29).
Paul shows how deep his humility goes: though he was in the form of God, he emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, and humbled himself to death on a cross (Philippians 2:6–8).

A yoke joins two animals so they pull together. Jesus does not lay a burden on us and leave; he walks beside us under the same yoke. Bring him your burden this week and learn from his gentle, humble heart. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: come to me when you are tired, and I will help you. Jesus is gentle and kind. Tell him what is hard for you.

homily: Dear friends, today we begin the Three Days' Fast, the fast of the Ninevites. Jonah walks into the great city of Nineveh and cries: forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown! And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:4–5).

Even the king rises from his throne and sits in ashes. And when God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity, and he did not do it (Jonah 3:10). God takes no pleasure in punishment; he delights in mercy.
Our Church has kept this fast for fifteen centuries. Many of us go to Kuravilangad and other shrines. But the heart of the fast is not the pilgrimage; it is turning from our evil ways.

In the Gospel Jesus calls Matthew from the tax booth and eats with sinners. He says: go and learn what this means, I desire mercy, not sacrifice. For I have come to call not the righteous but sinners (Matthew 9:13). Our fasting is not to make us proud, but to open us to mercy and make us merciful.
Today the Church Unity Octave also begins. Let our conversion help heal the wounds of division among Christians. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nineveh said sorry to God and fasted, and God forgave them! These three days, let us say sorry for something and give up a small treat.

homily: Dear friends, on the second day of our fast the readings teach us how to confess. Solomon prays at the dedication of the Temple: when your people sin and then turn, acknowledge your name and pray, then hear from heaven, and forgive (2 Chronicles 6:24–27).

Baruch gives words of confession to the exiles: the Lord our God is in the right, but there is open shame on us today (Baruch 1:15). True confession does not blame God or others. It simply says: I have sinned.

James gives the Church's practice: are any among you sick? They should call for the elders of the church. Confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed (James 5:14, 16). Here the Church has always seen the sacraments of Anointing and Reconciliation.

John the Baptist points to the One who takes sin away: here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world! (John 1:29). Our fasting does not remove sin; the Lamb does. Let the fast lead us to the confessional and to the Lamb. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the Lamb of God who takes away our sins. When we say sorry in confession, he makes our hearts clean and new!

homily: Dear friends, on the last day of our fast the readings are full of love. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her (Genesis 29:20). Love makes sacrifice light.

Hosea ends his book of warnings with tenderness: return, O Israel, to the LORD your God. I will heal their disloyalty; I will love them freely (Hosea 14:1, 4). The goal of the fast is not an empty stomach but a heart filled with God's love.

In the Gospel a woman known as a sinner weeps at Jesus' feet in Simon's house. Simon judges her. Jesus says: her sins, which were many, have been forgiven; hence she has shown great love (Luke 7:47). Her love is the sign of her forgiveness.

Peter says: above all, maintain constant love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins (1 Peter 4:8). Today we honour St Sebastian and pray for our bishops who bear his name. Let us end this fast as the woman did: at Jesus' feet, forgiven, and loving much. Amen.
kids: Children, a woman was very sorry for her sins and cried at Jesus' feet. Jesus forgave her, and she loved him so much! Let us love Jesus and our families today.

homily: Dear friends, the Three Days' Fast is over, and today the Church celebrates God's joy. Through Ezekiel God swears: as I live, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live (Ezekiel 33:11).

Micah sings: who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity? He delights in showing clemency. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea (Micah 7:18–19). What we brought to God in these three days, he has thrown into the sea.

In the Gospel Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one, and of a woman who searches her whole house for one coin. When they find them they say: rejoice with me. Just so, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:6–7).
John the Elder writes: I have no greater joy than this, to hear that my children are walking in the truth (3 John 4). Let the fruit of our fast be joy, and let us become seekers of the lost. Amen.
kids: Children, a shepherd found his lost sheep and was so happy! God is that happy when we come back to him. Thank God for these three days of fasting.

homily: Dear friends, on the third Friday of Denha we honour the four Evangelists. In Eden a river flows out to water the garden, and from there it divides and becomes four branches (Genesis 2:10). The Fathers saw here the four Gospels flowing from Christ to water the whole earth.
Ezekiel and Revelation describe four living creatures around God's throne: a human face, a lion, an ox and an eagle. Tradition gave them to Matthew, Mark, Luke and John: four faces, one Christ.

The Gospel is the parable of the sower. The seed is the word of God. Some falls on the path, some on rock, some among thorns. But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance (Luke 8:15).
The Evangelists have done their part: the seed has reached us. Now the question is our soil. Let us read a Gospel this month, and remove the thorns that choke the word. Amen.
kids: Children, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote down the story of Jesus for us! Let us read a little of the Gospel every day so that God's word grows in our hearts.

homily: Dear friends, Paul says salvation is not far away. We do not have to climb to heaven or go down into the abyss. The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart (Romans 10:8).
The faith that saves is simple: if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved (Romans 10:9). Lips and heart together.
And it is for everyone: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved (Romans 10:13). No distinction of race or past.

In the Gospel a leper kneels and says: if you choose, you can make me clean (Mark 1:40). He called on the Lord, and Jesus touched and healed him. However far we feel from God, he is near to anyone who calls. Let us say today with lips and heart: Jesus is Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul says anyone who calls on Jesus will be saved. Let us say it together now: Jesus is Lord!

homily: Dear friends, today two great calls are set side by side. Moses, a shepherd in the desert, sees a bush burning and not consumed, and hears: Moses, Moses! God reveals his name: I AM WHO I AM (Exodus 3:14).

Saul, on the road to Damascus, is thrown down by a light from heaven and hears: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? He asks: who are you, Lord? The answer: I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting (Acts 9:4–5). The God of the burning bush now has a human face, and he suffers in his Church.
Blind, Saul is led into Damascus. Ananias lays hands on him; something like scales fall from his eyes; he is baptized, and immediately proclaims Jesus as the Son of God.
Years later Paul writes: last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me. And: by the grace of God I am what I am (1 Corinthians 15:8, 10).

The Gospel explains this grace. Workers hired at five o'clock receive the same wage as those hired at dawn. The owner says: are you envious because I am generous? (Matthew 20:15). Paul came late and received the full wage of grace.
None of us earns salvation; all of us receive it. Let us give thanks for grace, rejoice in others' blessings, and pray today that all Christians may be one. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul started by hurting Christians, but Jesus changed him into his best messenger. God's love is for everyone, even people who come late!
Let us be happy when others get good things, because God is generous.

opts.a: Ananias, the disciple who was afraid
intro: Every conversion story has two heroes: the one who is converted, and the one who dares to welcome him. Today we look at Ananias.

points.apply: Tell God honestly what you fear about someone.

points.h: Go, for he is my chosen instrument
points.apply: Pray for someone you have written off.
Welcome a newcomer or a returning Catholic as brother or sister.

concl: Without Ananias there might have been no Paul.
God still needs disciples brave enough to say brother.
opts.resolve: This week I will reach out to one person I have been afraid of or have given up on.
homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate the conversion of Paul. But there is another hero in the story, a quiet disciple in Damascus named Ananias.

The Lord said to him: get up and go to the street called Straight, and look for a man of Tarsus named Saul. Ananias answered honestly: Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints (Acts 9:11, 13). He was afraid, and he had good reason to be.

But the Lord said: go, for he is an instrument whom I have chosen to bring my name before Gentiles and kings (Acts 9:15). God sees what we cannot see. The man everyone feared was the man God had chosen.
So Ananias went, laid his hands on Saul and said: Brother Saul (Acts 9:17). His first word was brother. Something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he was baptised.

Who is the Saul in my life? The person I fear, avoid, or have given up on? Perhaps God is sending me, as he sent Ananias, to say: brother, sister. And let us bring that person to the Holy Qurbana in our prayer today. Amen.

intro: Saul did not change his zeal, his intelligence or his energy. He changed his centre. Conversion is not becoming someone else but becoming who God meant.

points.apply: Name one thing you are proud of and offer it to Christ.
Make a good confession this week.

sub: Faith in the Son of God who loved me.
points.apply: Pray each morning: Lord, live in me today.

concl: Conversion keeps our gifts but changes our centre.
Paul's zeal became love for Christ and for all peoples.
opts.resolve: Each morning this week I will pray Galatians 2:20: it is Christ who lives in me.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, what changed when Saul became Paul? Not his intelligence: he remained a brilliant scholar. Not his energy: he remained tireless. Not his zeal: he remained on fire. What changed was the centre of his life.

He writes: whatever gains I had, these I have come to regard as loss because of Christ (Philippians 3:7). His birth, his learning, his religious record, all the things he had been proud of, he now laid at the feet of Christ.

He discovered that if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new (2 Corinthians 5:17). This is what happens in every good confession: the old passes, the new begins.

And he could finally say: it is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me (Galatians 2:20).

God does not want to destroy our gifts but to set them on the right centre. Let us offer him our pride, make a good confession, and pray each day: Lord, live in me. And receive him in the Holy Qurbana as Paul's whole life. Amen.

Dear friends, Paul thanks God for the Christians of Thessalonica, remembering your work of faith and labor of love and steadfastness of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ (1 Thessalonians 1:3). Faith that works, love that labours, hope that endures.

The Gospel came to them not in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit, and they received it with joy even in persecution (1 Thessalonians 1:5–6). Timothy, whom we honour today with Titus, was sent to strengthen them.
In the Gospel Jesus says: whoever is from God hears the words of God (John 8:47). Belonging to God is shown by listening to him.

Today India celebrates Republic Day. Let us thank God for our Constitution, which guarantees justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all, pray for those who govern, and be citizens whose faith works for the common good. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul was happy because the Christians worked hard, loved others and never gave up. Today let us pray for India and help someone in our town!

homily: Dear friends, Paul says: the appointed time has grown short; the present form of this world is passing away (1 Corinthians 7:29, 31). Christians hold this world's things lightly.

He praises those who give themselves wholly to the Lord, and says his aim is unhindered devotion to the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:35). The Church honours consecrated life as a sign of the Kingdom, and marriage as a holy vocation.

In the Gospel Martha is busy and Mary listens. Jesus says: Martha, Martha, you are worried and distracted by many things; there is need of only one thing (Luke 10:41–42). He corrects not her service but her anxiety.
The one thing necessary is Christ. Whatever our vocation, let us keep a place every day at his feet. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary sat and listened to Jesus. Jesus said that was the best thing to do! Let us spend a little quiet time with Jesus today.

homily: Dear friends, Paul reminds the Galatians that God's promise to Abraham came long before the law, and the law cannot cancel it. And the promise was made to Abraham's offspring, that is, to one person, who is Christ (Galatians 3:16). The whole story of Israel moves toward Jesus.
In the Gospel Martha meets Jesus four days after Lazarus died: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:21). She brings both grief and faith.

Jesus answers: I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live (John 11:25). And Martha confesses: Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God (John 11:27).

St Thomas Aquinas, whom we honour today, gave his great mind to this faith and ended in adoration of Christ in the Eucharist, the pledge of our resurrection. Let us bring our sorrows to Jesus and say with Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told Martha: I am the resurrection and the life! Martha said: Yes, Lord, I believe! Let us say it too.

homily: Dear friends, today's readings trace a line of innocent blood. God says to Cain: listen; your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground! (Genesis 4:10). Naboth is falsely accused and stoned for refusing to give up his ancestral vineyard.
Stephen too is falsely accused, yet his face shines like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). He sees the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.

As the stones fall he prays: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:59–60). These are the words of Jesus on the cross: Father, forgive them; and to the thief: today you will be with me in Paradise (Luke 23:43).

Hebrews says Jesus' blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel: not vengeance but forgiveness. Saul held the coats of Stephen's killers; Stephen's prayer was answered when Saul became Paul. Let us forgive, and see heaven opened. Amen.
kids: Children, St Stephen loved Jesus so much that he forgave the people who hurt him. When someone hurts us, let us pray for them like Stephen did.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Ephesians: we are members of one another. So speak the truth, and let no evil talk come out of your mouths, but only what is useful for building up.
He adds: be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:26). Anger kept overnight becomes bitterness.
In the Gospel Jesus teaches the Our Father, and then comments on only one line: if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14).

Every Our Father is a promise to forgive. Today, the eve of the Lord's Day, let us be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven us (Ephesians 4:32). Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul says: do not stay angry when the sun goes down! Before you sleep tonight, say sorry and forgive.

intro: Theme: “You are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
The Holy Name at the start of the year: called by name, saved, exalted.

sub: A new name, a new mission.
q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
points.apply: Learn the meaning of your baptismal name and thank God for it.

sub: Call on him in every need.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved;
She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer each morning this year.

q: To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.
Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
points.apply: Never use the Lord's name carelessly; bow your head when you hear it.

concl: The year begins with the Name that saves.
With Mary, Mother of God, let us carry this Name into every day.
2027-01-01.resolve: Consecrate the new year to Jesus tonight as a family.

intro: Theme: “Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
Near God we shine, listen, and offer ourselves.

points.h: Near God, we shine and listen
q: Now the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”

And all of us, with unveiled faces, seeing the glory of the Lord as though reflected in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another; for this comes from the Lord, the Spirit.
points.apply: Begin each prayer this week with Samuel's words.

q: One thing I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple.
He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
points.apply: Visit the church on a weekday this week.

q: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
points.apply: Children obey promptly; parents listen patiently.

q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
I appeal to you therefore, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: Offer your work each morning as a sacrifice to God.

concl: Like Jesus, we belong in the Father's house, and we sanctify our homes by obedience.
St Chavara shows this joined together: prayer, family, education.
2027-01-03.resolve: Prepare for Denha on Wednesday with a family prayer and confession.

intro: Theme: “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
Denha: the dawn of the Trinity's revelation and of our Baptism.

q: Now Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke, because the LORD had descended upon it in fire; the smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, while the whole mountain shook violently.
And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silent adoration today.

q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.
And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
points.apply: Make the Sign of the Cross slowly and with faith each time you pray.

sub: Fulfilled in Christ and the Church.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
For this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is within you through the laying on of my hands;
points.apply: Use one gift of God to serve others this month.

q: For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.
but it has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
points.apply: Find your baptismal date and celebrate it.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opened, and it has not closed.
We are baptised: let us live as the Father's beloved.
2027-01-06.resolve: Keep holy water at home and bless your family each night.

intro: Theme: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he.”
The name of God revealed at the bush, in Jesus, and on the Cross.

sub: He sends Moses to set his people free.
q: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” He said further, “Thus you shall say to the Israelites, ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
I told you that you would die in your sins, for you will die in your sins unless you believe that I am he.”
points.apply: Make an act of faith each morning this week.

q: For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.
He said to them, “You are from below, I am from above; you are of this world, I am not of this world.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes in silence before God this week.

sub: The Cross reveals the I AM.
q: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon a pole; and whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live.
So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but I speak these things as the Father instructed me.
points.apply: Place a crucifix where you see it every day.

sub: Who is, who was, who is to come.
He loves us and frees us.
q: Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, the LORD of hosts: I am the first and I am the last; besides me there is no god.
“I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty.
points.apply: Begin and end each day with the Glory Be.

concl: The One who is has come close in Jesus.
His name shines brightest on the Cross.
2027-01-10.resolve: Adore the Lord for ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

intro: Theme: “Do not fear, for I am with you.”
Chosen by God, called by Jesus, pressing on toward the goal.

q: Be strong and bold; have no fear or dread of them, because it is the LORD your God who goes with you; he will not fail you or forsake you.”
You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last, so that the Father will give you whatever you ask him in my name.
points.apply: Face one fear this week trusting that God goes before you.

q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
He went up the mountain and called to him those whom he wanted, and they came to him.
points.apply: Thank God each morning that he has chosen you.

q: Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire other than you.

More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I regard them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ
points.apply: Give up one thing during the Three Days' Fast.

q: Do not remember the former things, or consider the things of old. I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.

Beloved, I do not consider that I have made it my own; but this one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Let go of a past failure and begin again.

concl: God chooses, calls and goes before us.
The chosen press on, starting with the fast of the Ninevites.
2027-01-17.resolve: Keep the Three Days' Fast faithfully this week.

intro: Theme: “A spring of water gushing up to eternal life.”
Christ revealed at the well: meeting, living water, true worship, mission.

q: As a deer longs for flowing streams, so my soul longs for you, O God. My soul thirsts for God, for the living God. When shall I come and behold the face of God?
A Samaritan woman came to draw water, and Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”
points.apply: Bring your thirst to God in prayer today.

q: for my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and dug out cisterns for themselves, cracked cisterns that can hold no water.
but those who drink of the water that I will give them will never be thirsty. The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.”
points.apply: Name one cracked cistern and turn from it.

q: It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to restore the survivors of Israel; I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.”
Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one who is speaking to you.”
points.apply: Pray for people of other faiths in your neighbourhood.

q: but those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
points.apply: Tell one person what Christ means to you.

concl: Christ meets us at our wells of thirst.
Drink the living water, then run and tell.
2027-01-24.resolve: Cross one barrier of prejudice this week.

intro: Theme: “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
Forgiveness revealed: costly, merciful, given by Christ through his Church.

q: He shall do with the bull just as is done with the bull of sin offering; he shall do the same with this. The priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
points.apply: Thank Christ for the price of your forgiveness.

q: To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him,
“Why does this fellow speak in this way? It is blasphemy! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
points.apply: Pray for the sins of your family and community.

q: A friend loves at all times, and kinsfolk are born to share adversity.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Carry someone to Christ in prayer or help.

q: I, I am He who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain the sins of any, they are retained.”
points.apply: Go to confession this week.

concl: In Denha Christ is revealed as the one who forgives.
Receive his forgiveness, and carry others to him.
2027-01-31.resolve: Make a good confession before the end of the week.

intro: Theme: “She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.”
Anna's faithfulness and the Child's growth.

sub: Fasting and prayer night and day.
q: Evening and morning and at noon I utter my complaint and moan, and he will hear my voice.
then as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.
points.apply: Keep a fixed time of prayer every day this year.

sub: She comes at that very moment.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
points.apply: Speak about Jesus to one person this week.

q: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.
God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
points.apply: Choose one spiritual book to read this year.

concl: Old Anna and the young Child both show a life full of God.
Faithful prayer becomes joyful witness.
2027-01-02.resolve: Thank an elderly person for their prayers this week.

intro: Theme: “This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.”
The Son one with the Father; believers born of God.

sub: Love for the Father includes his children.
q: Is not he your father, who created you, who made you and established you?
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the parent loves the child.
points.apply: Thank God today for your Baptism.

points.h: The Son does the Father's works
sub: Honour the Son as the Father.
q: then I was beside him, like a master worker; and I was daily his delight, rejoicing before him always,
Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
points.apply: Pray the Glory Be with full attention each time today.

q: With the LORD on my side I do not fear. What can mortals do to me?
for whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.
points.apply: Make an act of faith whenever fear rises.

concl: The Child is the eternal Son, worthy of all honour.
Born of God, we share his victory.
2027-01-04.resolve: Prepare for Denha by renewing your baptismal promises.

intro: Theme: “We are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.”
Servant and Son; the unknown one among us.

sub: A witness to what would come.
q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Now Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant, to testify to the things that would be spoken later.
points.apply: Thank God for a faithful servant who taught you the faith.

points.h: Christ the Son; we are his house
sub: The builder is greater than the house.
Christ is the Son and heir.
We are the house if we hold firm.
q: He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
Christ, however, was faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.
points.apply: Make one change at home that makes it more a house of God.

points.h: One whom you do not know
sub: The hidden one stands among us.
q: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill be made low; the uneven ground shall become level, and the rough places a plain.
John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, the one who is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal.”
points.apply: Light a lamp tonight and pray for those who do not know Christ.

concl: Tomorrow the hidden one is revealed at the Jordan.
Let us be his house, lit and ready.
2027-01-05.resolve: Keep the Denha eve with a lamp and family prayer.

intro: Theme: “Christ is proclaimed in every way… and in that I rejoice.”
Joy without rivalry: Paul in chains, John the friend of the bridegroom.

q: Even though you intended to do harm to me, God intended it for good, in order to preserve a numerous people, as he is doing today.
I want you to know, beloved, that what has happened to me has actually helped to spread the gospel,
points.apply: Offer one hardship today for the Gospel.

q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!”
What does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether out of false motives or true; and in that I rejoice.
points.apply: Pray for a fellow worker you envy.

q: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, he also exalts.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of service this week.

concl: In the season of Denha, Christ is to be manifested, not we.
Joy in his glory heals envy.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you.”
The Baptist and the prophets: courage for the truth, held by God.

q: Nathan said to David, “You are the man! Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul;
For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, because John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
points.apply: Accept one correction this week without defending yourself.

sub: John filled with the Spirit before birth.
God's call is older than our fears.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He must never drink wine or strong drink; even before his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Pray for unborn children and for the vocations God has prepared.

q: They will fight against you; but they shall not prevail against you, for I am with you, says the LORD, to deliver you.
While Peter was kept in prison, the church prayed fervently to God for him.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for the persecuted Church.

concl: The Baptist's courage still speaks.
Truth with love, held by God's promise: I am with you.
2027-01-08.resolve: Speak one hard truth this week, gently and with love.

intro: Theme: “Are you the one who is to come?”
John's question, Jesus' answer, heaven's song.

q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
and sent them to the Lord to ask, “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?”
points.apply: Bring one honest question to Jesus in prayer.

sub: Blessed is the one not offended.
q: the LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.

And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy today.

sub: We join them at the Qurbana.
q: And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”

And the four living creatures, each of them with six wings, are full of eyes all around and inside. Day and night without ceasing they sing, “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come.”
points.apply: Sing the Holy, holy, holy at Qurbana with full attention tomorrow.

concl: Christ answers doubt with mercy and lifts our eyes to his throne.
He is the one who is to come.
2027-01-09.resolve: Prepare for Sunday by spending time before the Blessed Sacrament.

intro: Theme: “The one who comes from above is above all.”
Christ, head over all, seen with the eyes of the heart.

q: Open my eyes, so that I may behold wondrous things out of your law.
so that, with the eyes of your heart enlightened, you may know what is the hope to which he has called you, what are the riches of his glorious inheritance among the saints,
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit for enlightened eyes each morning.

sub: Head of the Church, his Body.
q: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
And he has put all things under his feet and has made him the head over all things for the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all.
points.apply: Pray for the unity of the Church this week.

q: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of the hand? Who has wrapped up the waters in a garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is the person's name? And what is the name of the person's child? Surely you know!
The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever disobeys the Son will not see life, but must endure God's wrath.
points.apply: Give Christ the first moment of each day.

concl: Faith sees Christ above all.
Let him be first in our lives as he is first in heaven.
2027-01-11.resolve: Begin each day this week with five minutes of prayer before anything else.

intro: Theme: “See what love the Father has given us.”
Children of God, freed by the Son who destroys the works of the devil.

sub: The world does not know us.
q: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
See what love the Father has given us, that we should be called children of God; and that is what we are. The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know him.
points.apply: Thank the Father for your Baptism today.

points.h: The works of the devil destroyed
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
Everyone who commits sin is a child of the devil; for the devil has been sinning from the beginning. The Son of God was revealed for this purpose, to destroy the works of the devil.
points.apply: Renounce one sinful habit today in Jesus' name.

q: You will tread on the lion and the adder, the young lion and the serpent you will trample under foot.
But Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him!”
points.apply: Pray the St Michael prayer each night this week.

concl: We are children of God, freed by the Son.
Live as who you are.
2027-01-12.resolve: Say each morning: I am a child of God; and live it.

intro: Theme: “Do whatever he tells you.”
Cana: Mary's intercession, Jesus' glory, the wedding of the Lamb.

q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines, of rich food filled with marrow, of well-aged wines strained clear.
When the wine gave out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.”
points.apply: Tell Mary the need of one family you know.

q: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread. Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph; what he says to you, do.”
His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
points.apply: Obey one word of Jesus today.

q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
And the angel said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.” And he said to me, “These are true words of God.”
points.apply: Prepare for Holy Communion with a short prayer each time.

concl: At Cana the glory of Jesus is revealed through Mary's care.
Do whatever he tells you, and the water of life becomes wine.
2027-01-13.resolve: Pray one decade of the Rosary daily this week for families in need.

intro: Theme: “Glorify God in your body.”
The Father's house, the temple of Christ's body, and our bodies as temples.

q: It is zeal for your house that has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”
points.apply: Keep silence and reverence in church this Sunday.

sub: God meets us in the risen Christ.
q: The latter splendor of this house shall be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts; and in this place I will give prosperity, says the LORD of hosts.
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
points.apply: Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament this week.

q: Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.

Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God, and that you are not your own? For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.
points.apply: Give up one habit that harms your body.

concl: Christ's body is the true Temple; ours are temples of his Spirit.
St Devasahayam made his body an offering for Christ.
2027-01-14.resolve: Honour God's house and your body as his temple this week.

intro: Theme: “Lord, you know that I love you.”
Peter and Paul: grace transforms a denier and a persecutor into pillars of the Church.

q: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.

When they had finished breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my lambs.”
points.apply: Tell Jesus in your own words that you love him.

q: Listen to me, O coastlands, pay attention, you peoples from far away! The LORD called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.

But when God, who had set me apart before I was born and called me through his grace, was pleased to reveal his Son to me, so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles, I did not confer with any human being,
points.apply: Thank God for a grace that changed your life.

points.h: A priestly people for all nations
q: but you shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall speak to the Israelites.”
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
points.apply: Pray for the Pope and our Major Archbishop daily this week.

concl: Christ builds his Church on forgiven sinners who love him.
Peter and Paul show what grace can do.
2027-01-15.resolve: Answer Jesus each morning: Lord, you know that I love you.

intro: Theme: “Learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart.”
Revelation to the little, the self-emptying Son, the yoke that gives rest.

q: But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; my soul is like the weaned child that is with me.
At that time Jesus said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants;
points.apply: Pray like a child today, simply and trustingly.

sub: Took the form of a slave.
q: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth.
Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as something to be exploited,
points.apply: Do one hidden act of service today.

q: I will satisfy the weary, and all who are faint I will replenish.

Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
points.apply: Bring your heaviest burden to Jesus in prayer.

concl: The revealed Lord shows us a gentle and humble heart.
Come to him and find rest.
2027-01-16.resolve: Spend five minutes each evening this week placing your burdens before Jesus.

intro: Theme: “God changed his mind… and he did not do it.”
The fast of the Ninevites: turning to God, who delights in mercy.

q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
The people of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and see, something greater than Jonah is here!
points.apply: Keep the three days' fast as fully as you can.

q: When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, God changed his mind about the calamity that he had said he would bring upon them; and he did not do it.
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Turn from one specific sin today.

q: and return to the LORD your God, and you and your children obey him with all your heart and with all your soul, just as I am commanding you today, then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you, gathering you again from all the peoples among whom the LORD your God has scattered you.
Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
points.apply: Give the food you save to the poor.

concl: Nineveh's fast opened the way to mercy.
Our fast too must lead to conversion and mercy.
2027-01-18.resolve: Make a good confession during the three days.

intro: Theme: “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!”
Confession, healing and the Lamb who removes sin.

q: And you shall say: The Lord our God is in the right, but there is open shame on us today, on the people of Judah, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective.
points.apply: Make your confession during these three days.

q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
The next day he saw Jesus coming toward him and declared, “Here is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
points.apply: Look at the Host with faith at Communion.

q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak, but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed them with justice.
you should know that whoever brings back a sinner from wandering will save the sinner's soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
points.apply: Reach out gently to someone who has left the Church.

concl: The fast prepares us; the Lamb forgives us.
Confess, pray for one another, bring back the wanderer.
2027-01-19.resolve: Make a good confession before the fast ends.

intro: Theme: “She has shown great love.”
The fast ends in love: God loves freely; the forgiven love much.

points.h: Return; I will love them freely
q: I will heal their disloyalty; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned from them.
Then he said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Thank God tonight for his free love.

q: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her.
Above all, maintain constant love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins.
points.apply: Do one costly act of love today.

q: But I said, “I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my cause is with the LORD, and my reward with my God.”
“Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven;
points.apply: Do not hide your faith this week.

concl: The fast ends not in hunger but in love.
Forgiven much, let us love much.
2027-01-20.resolve: Break the fast with an act of love for someone lonely.

intro: Theme: “Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.”
After the fast: the God who delights in mercy, and the joy of the found.

q: Say to them, As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live; turn back, turn back from your evil ways; for why will you die, O house of Israel?
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some think of slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.
points.apply: Thank God for his patience with you.

q: He will again have compassion upon us; he will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.

When he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders and rejoices. And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.’
points.apply: Do not dig up sins God has forgiven.

q: The LORD, your God, is in your midst, a warrior who gives victory; he will rejoice over you with gladness, he will renew you in his love; he will exult over you with loud singing
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Reach out to one person who has drifted away.

concl: The fast ends in God's joy.
Let us rejoice, and seek the lost.
2027-01-21.resolve: Pray this week for one person far from God, by name.

intro: Theme: “Hold it fast in an honest and good heart.”
The four Evangelists and the soil of our hearts.

q: A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides and becomes four branches.
But these are written so that you may come to believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that through believing you may have life in his name.
points.apply: Thank God for the Gospels and those who brought them to Kerala.

q: As for the appearance of their faces: the four had the face of a human being, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and the face of an eagle;
the first living creature like a lion, the second living creature like an ox, the third living creature with a face like a human face, and the fourth living creature like a flying eagle.
points.apply: Read the first chapter of each Gospel this week.

q: Your words were found, and I ate them, and your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart; for I am called by your name, O LORD, God of hosts.
But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
points.apply: Remove one thorn that chokes God's word.

concl: The Evangelists sowed; we must be good soil.
Read, keep and bear fruit.
2027-01-22.resolve: Read one Gospel chapter every day for the rest of January.

intro: Theme: “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
The near word, the saving confession, the leper who called.

sub: On your lips and in your heart.
q: No, the word is very near to you; it is in your mouth and in your heart for you to observe.
But what does it say? “The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart” (that is, the word of faith that we proclaim);
points.apply: Memorise Romans 10:9 this week.

q: Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Say aloud each day: Jesus, you are Lord.

q: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
A leper came to him begging him, and kneeling he said to him, “If you choose, you can make me clean.”
points.apply: Bring your deepest need to Jesus in prayer today.

concl: Salvation is near to anyone who calls.
Lips and heart together confess: Jesus is Lord.
2027-01-23.resolve: Pray the name of Jesus whenever you are tempted or afraid this week.

intro: Theme: “By the grace of God I am what I am.”
Two calls by name, and the generous wage of grace.

q: When the LORD saw that he had turned aside to see, God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”
He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?”
points.apply: Answer God today: Here I am.

q: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” He said further, “Thus you shall say to the Israelites, ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
He asked, “Who are you, Lord?” The reply came, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
points.apply: Treat the Church as the Body of Christ.

q: What shall I return to the LORD for all his bounty to me?
But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me has not been in vain. On the contrary, I worked harder than any of them—though it was not I, but the grace of God that is with me.
points.apply: List three graces you did not earn.

q: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the LORD.
Am I not allowed to do what I choose with what belongs to me? Or are you envious because I am generous?’
points.apply: Rejoice in someone else's blessing.

concl: God calls by name and gives grace beyond merit.
Let gratitude replace envy, and unity replace division.
2027-01-25.resolve: Pray daily this week for Christian unity.

intro: Theme: “Whoever is from God hears the words of God.”
Faith, love and hope at work, the word received with joy, and faithful citizenship.

q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
remembering before our God and Father your work of faith and labor of love and steadfastness of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Do one labour of love for your neighbourhood.

q: How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth!
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, for in spite of persecution you received the word with joy inspired by the Holy Spirit,
points.apply: Read the day's Gospel with joy each morning.

q: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a reproach to any people.
Whoever is from God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear them is that you are not from God.”
points.apply: Pray for India and its leaders today.

concl: Faith works, love labours, hope endures.
God's people listen to God and serve the nation.
2027-01-26.resolve: Serve the common good in one concrete way this week.

intro: Theme: “There is need of only one thing.”
The passing world, undivided devotion, and the better part.

q: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven:
I say this for your own benefit, not to put any restraint upon you, but to promote good order and unhindered devotion to the Lord.
points.apply: Give up one distraction this week for prayer.

q: Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved.
But the Lord answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried and distracted by many things;
points.apply: Hand one worry to Jesus each morning.

q: One thing I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple.
there is need of only one thing. Mary has chosen the better part, which will not be taken away from her.”
points.apply: Spend ten minutes daily in silent listening to the Gospel.

concl: The world passes; Christ remains.
Every vocation needs a place at the Lord's feet.
2027-01-27.resolve: Keep ten minutes of silence with the Gospel each day this week.

intro: Theme: “I am the resurrection and the life.”
The promise fulfilled in Christ, Martha's faith in sorrow, and St Thomas Aquinas.

q: and by your offspring shall all the nations of the earth gain blessing for themselves, because you have obeyed my voice.”
Now the promises were made to Abraham and to his offspring; it does not say, “And to offsprings,” as of many; but it says, “And to your offspring,” that is, to one person, who is Christ.
points.apply: Thank God for a promise he has kept in your life.

points.h: Lord, if you had been here
q: The LORD is near to the brokenhearted, and saves the crushed in spirit.
Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
points.apply: Bring one sorrow honestly to Jesus.

q: And you shall know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people.
She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.”
points.apply: Pray Martha's creed each morning this week.

concl: Every promise of God meets in Christ.
He is the resurrection; let us answer with Martha: I believe.
2027-01-28.resolve: Visit or call a grieving family this week.

intro: Theme: “Today you will be with me in Paradise.”
Innocent blood, the martyr's vision, and forgiveness like Christ's.

q: And the LORD said, “What have you done? Listen; your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground!
and to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
points.apply: Speak up for someone treated unjustly.

q: But Naboth said to Ahab, “The LORD forbid that I should give you my ancestral inheritance.”
And all who sat in the council looked intently at him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
points.apply: Stay calm and faithful when criticised for your faith.

points.h: Do not hold this sin against them
q: Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his faithful ones.
Then he knelt down and cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” When he had said this, he died.
points.apply: Pray by name for someone who has wronged you.

concl: Christ's blood and the martyr's prayer speak forgiveness.
Forgiveness opens heaven and plants the Church.
2027-01-29.resolve: Pray each day this week for persecuted Christians.

intro: Theme: “Forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”
Speech that builds, anger that does not last, and the Our Father's condition.

q: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, but only what is useful for building up, as there is need, so that your words may give grace to those who hear.
points.apply: Say only words that build up today.

q: When you are disturbed, do not sin; ponder it on your beds, and be silent.
Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger,
points.apply: Make peace with someone before bedtime.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly, naming someone to forgive.

concl: We are one body; let our words and hearts build it up.
Forgive before the sun sets, and pray as forgiven children.
2027-01-30.resolve: Never go to bed angry this week.
